articles.title: Tokenomics at scale: Track and cap Amazon Bedrock spend per IAM principal with CUR 2.0 and AWS Budgets
articles.content: Generative AI spend is hard to attribute. Before an organization expands AI access, CFOs and CTOs usually want three answers: what do we spend per person or per team, can we cap it, and how much work does it take to get there. In our previous post, Tokenomics at Scale: How Jamf Built Real-Time Spend Enforcement for Amazon Bedrock , we explained a custom enforcement loop built on AWS IAM Identity Center , Amazon Athena over Amazon Bedrock model invocation logs , and AWS Lambda . This approach gives near-real-time control, but it requires code you then own and operate. This post shows how to get per-identity Amazon Bedrock cost visibility and enforceable spend limits using only AWS-native features, with no application code to write for the common case. The approach relies on three things: IAM principal attribution , which Amazon Bedrock records automatically; AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) 2.0 or AWS Cost Explorer for reporting; and AWS Budgets with budget actions for enforcement. By the end, you will have per-identity cost reporting and an automatic guardrail that restricts Amazon Bedrock access when a threshold is crossed. Solution overview The solution has three parts: attribute, report, and enforce. Attribute. Amazon Bedrock captures the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) principal identity, the IAM user or role , for every inference request. This happens automatically, with no change to your Amazon Bedrock model inference calls. If several people share one role, you add per-user detail with session tags passed at role assumption time. If each person or application has its own role, principal tags on the role are enough. Report. Activate those tags as cost allocation tags, then read the data either in Cost Explorer for a console-only view, or in a CUR 2.0 data export for detailed line-item analysis and SQL queries. Enforce. Create an AWS Budget scoped to Amazon Bedrock and filtered to one identity or tag value, then attach a budget action that applies a Deny IAM policy when the threshold is crossed. The following sections show each part in more detail, alongside the implementation steps. Prerequisites To deploy this solution, you need: An AWS account with Amazon Bedrock model access enabled. Permissions to tag IAM principal , activate cost allocation tags , create data exports , and create budgets and budget actions. Amazon Bedrock accessed through IAM roles or IAM users. AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) configured with appropriate credentials. A CUR 2.0 data export and an Amazon Simple Storage Service ( Amazon S3 ) bucket to receive it. (optional, for detailed line-item analysis) . Amazon Athena. (optional, for querying the export) . AWS Billing Console access is managed separately from most IAM permissions. Confirm you have it before starting. Walkthrough Before configuring anything, check what you already have. Amazon Bedrock records caller identity for every inference request automatically. Open Cost Explorer, filter Service to Amazon Bedrock, and group by the available identity or tag dimension. For accounts where each application or person already uses a distinct IAM role, this may be all the visibility you need. To configure additional visibility: Step 1 gives you identity-level visibility. Steps 2 through 4 add tag dimensions and detailed reporting. Step 5 adds enforcement. Step 1: Decide how identity maps to your users How you tag depends on how your IAM principals are organized. One role per person or per application. Attach principal tags directly to each IAM role or user. These are static and apply to every request from that principal. Use the IAM console, or the AWS CLI: aws iam tag-role \ --role-name BedrockDeveloperRole-alice \ --tags Key=user,Value=alice@example.com Key=team,Value=platform Key=CostCenter,Value=CC-1001 A shared role used by several people, or a gateway. Principal tags cannot distinguish users on a shared role, because every session carries the same tags. Use session tags instead,…

The brand put together a visually stunning event space, packed with demos highlighting many of the different workflows users might experience when using Android XR smart glasses: preparing recipe shopping lists, creating music playlists, and even getting workout tips.

articles.title: Mozilla Firefox VPN has unlimited data until January 31, 2027, to fight back against Chrome and Edge, but is it already too late?
articles.content: Mozilla removes Firefox's free VPN data restrictions until January 31, 2027 Firefox users get unlimited VPN data without purchasing another subscription Firefox's free VPN protects browsing activity on shared Wi-Fi networks Mozilla has removed the monthly data restriction on Firefox's free VPN, giving desktop and Android users unlimited browsing protection through January 31, 2027. The temporary offer began November 10, 2026, and requires only a Mozilla account, without asking users to purchase an additional subscription. Mozilla is trying to make Firefox more attractive as it competes with Chrome and Edge, which held 68.79% and 5.36% of the global browser market, respectively, in October 2026. Firefox removes restrictions on its free VPN service The extended allowance gives Firefox users an opportunity to browse through shared Wi-Fi connections without exhausting their monthly VPN data allocation during the promotional period. This matters particularly during holiday travel, when passengers frequently depend on airport terminals, hotels, restaurants, and other public internet connections. Mozilla says its integrated free VPN conceals browsing activity from operators of shared networks while making it harder for websites to determine someone's location. The service also obscures users' IP addresses, reducing opportunities for websites to associate separate browsing sessions through their network addresses. “Most importantly, you’re not trading your browsing data for that protection,” said Mozilla, explaining its approach to privacy within the free VPN service. The company also says it does not monetize users' browsing information through advertising or maintain records identifying the websites they visit. However, unlimited data should not be confused with complete anonymity, because websites can still recognize visitors through cookies and accounts. Firefox's built-in protection also does not erase browsing records stored locally, meaning users must consider Private Windows for additional privacy. Availability comes with some limitations Availability is limited by platform and geographical restrictions, so users must check regional eligibility before expecting access. The complimentary service currently supports Firefox desktop and Android installations, but the company says iOS support is coming. Another restriction concerns application coverage, since the complimentary VPN protects internet activity inside Firefox rather than every application installed on devices. Mozilla directs customers seeking device-wide protection toward its separate Mozilla VPN product, which requires a paid subscription. Getting started requires signing into a Mozilla account, selecting the VPN control in Firefox's desktop toolbar, and completing the activation instructions. Android users can access the feature through the browser's three-dot menu, followed by Settings and the VPN configuration section. The timing allows Mozilla to attract privacy-conscious users, although a temporary allowance alone cannot guarantee sustained growth against established rivals. Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge retain substantial advantages through their established user bases, existing services, and integration with their respective technology ecosystems. Mozilla therefore needs more than a temporary privacy promotion if it expects dissatisfied Chrome and Edge users to consider switching browsers. Removing the data ceiling makes Firefox's complimentary protection more appealing, particularly for people who regularly depend on shared connections. However, whether those users remain after the promotional period depends partly on the service's future restrictions and Mozilla's ability to maintain interest.

articles.title: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Hydrogen, finally replacing 3.8 Flash
articles.content: Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen . These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen's purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google's ecosystem use. With Google's recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. The limits for Hydrogen are much more relaxed, with access beginning immediately. This model has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company's products. Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it's 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces "fabricated claims" by more than 5x, according to Google's analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash's score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Google brings Gemini 4 Hydrogen to Search with smarter answers and better visuals
articles.content: TL;DR Google is rolling out Gemini 4 Hydrogen to Search users worldwide, promising smarter, more relevant answers. Search can now better understand complicated questions, multiple requests, and typos while finding information from a wider range of websites. You can expect more visual responses, including images, comparison tables, and interactive tools across all AI Mode-supported languages. Google Search is getting a major upgrade, and it could noticeably change how you find information online. Google is rolling out Gemini 4 Hydrogen to all users worldwide, bringing smarter answers, better visuals, and a better understanding of even the most complicated questions. One of the biggest changes is that you won’t have to be quite as careful about how you phrase your searches. Whether you’re asking several questions at once, making a few typos, or looking for something very specific, Google says Search will be better at figuring out what you actually need.

articles.title: Ukraine says it can’t stop Russian strikes because Starshield is limited again
articles.content: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said today that Starshield has again been disabled on fast-moving drones in Ukrainian territory occupied by Russian forces, and that the US has provided "very little" information about the return of the restriction. "We have detected speed restrictions on Starshield on our Ukrainian territory again, in the temporarily occupied parts of Ukraine," Zelenskyy said in a speech at the 9th European Political Community Summit in Ireland. "The speed limit is back at 161 kilometers per hour—that’s 100 miles per hour." Zelenskyy's allegation is that Starshield—the military variant of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service—stops working on Ukrainian military drones when they travel above 161 kilometers per hour. articles.title: Microsoft Outlook is down for many: Here's what we know
articles.content: Microsoft Outlook might be down for many. Reports of outages from across the US started coming in around 12:30 PM ET. On DownDetector, there are over 120,000 concurrent reports. Other connected services like Microsoft Teams. Microsoft 365, Copilot, and Ondreive are also gettign reports. More tellingly,. we could not open Microsoft's own services status ((https://status.cloud.microsoft/) page to check on the status of Microsoft services. Microsoft's cloud services, Azure, also had reports of service issues, which may account for the wide-spread nature of these outages. On social media, people have bene reporting their inability to reach the services like Outlook. On X (formerly Twitter) is where we saw evidence that the outage may extend globally. Follow along as we track this continuing, and apparently widespread Outlook outage. Our first indication that something was awry with Outlook was on Downdetector, which noted a sharp rise in reports of service outages for Outlook. Microsoft 365, Microsoft Store, Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams, OneDrive, and Microsoft Azure. It's worth noting that users report these issues to Downdetector. Microsoft has yet to comment or confirm any of this. We've contacted Microsoft for comment and will update this live blog when they reply. (Image credit: Future) November 12, 2026 – 2:11 PM Not everything is offline There are some indications that the situation is worsening. While we were able to access OneDrive online 30 minutes ago, the site is no longer responding. The pain is being felt by individuals and organizations, such as universities, where entire email systems are now inaccessible. (Image credit: Future) November 12, 2026 – 2:15 PM When one service catches a cold... A look at DownDetector indicates that it's not just Outlook and Microsoft services that are struggling. However, these user-based reports can be misleading. Sometimes when people can't access one service connected to larger services, they assume it's their local one. We checked, for instance, AWS's status page and found no widespread reports of outages. (Image credit: Future) November 12, 2026 – 2:19 PM Microsoft knows A Microsoft 365 support account has acknowledged the issues across "the Americas" and wrote, "We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543." So they're investigating, but there's no news of a fix, just that they're working to mitigate it. We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543. November 12, 2026 November 12, 2026 – 2:25 PM What, we work? Millions rely on Microsoft tools like Outlook and OneDrive to get work done. When they're offline, well, as you can see below, things kind of slow down. When Outlook stops working…I stop working too https://t.co/LYVTTTA1TJ November 12, 2026 November 12, 2026 – 2:27 PM We're still not here By 2:25 PM ET, DownDetector was showing a small slowdown in outage reports across Microsoft services, but social media is still filled with posts about the ongoing Outlook outage that is across the US and the rest of the Americas. (Image credit: Future) November 12, 2026 – 2:31 PM Some perspective Sure, millions can't access work and personal emails, but they still have social media where they can complain or at least take their minds off the fact that a huge chunk of Microsoft products are currently not functioning. As this X user notes, at least social media isn't out. The MS Outlook outage is annoying and everything, but at least it isn't Instagram. articles.title: Everything you wanted to know about Nvidia but were too afraid to ask
articles.content: If you’re not in the tech world, you might only have been vaguely aware of Nvidia—and CEO Jensen Huang’s leather jackets —until he admitted to having an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy . On November 12, a day after revelations of a second affair, this one with an Nvidia executive, Huang resigned. Here’s why the company’s future could affect the entire AI industry. What Nvidia does Nvidia is at the center of the AI boom, as the world’s largest supplier of chips used in AI data centers. By some estimates, the company controls 80% of the market . As of November 3, it was the most valuable company in the world , with a market cap of around $5 trillion. By the morning of November 12, as Nvidia’s stock continued to plummet, that figure dropped to $4 trillion. (Huang’s own net worth had fallen $7.4 billion by that point.) Huang and cofounders Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem launched the company in 1993 . They started making graphics processing units, better known as GPUs, for video games. In 2006, they rolled out a platform that enabled other uses for GPUs. In 2012, researchers used the company’s chips to train AlexNet, a breakthrough AI program that taught computers how to recognize images. By the time that ChatGPT launched, Nvidia’s tech was fundamental to AI development. A large data center might have tens of thousands of Nvidia GPUs that run calculations to train AI models and generate responses when you type a question into ChatGPT or Claude. Training a new AI model could sometimes involve as many as 100,000 GPUs running at the same time for months. After the model is trained, the GPUs are used for “inference,” or applying the trained model to, say, rewrite your email or draw a cartoon of your cat. Inference also requires huge numbers of GPUs given that millions of people use AI at the same time. (In the U.S., around 60 million people use AI chatbots every day, according to a Pew survey this summer.) Nvidia systems also include CPUs (central processing units) that coordinate tasks and run operating systems in data centers, along with networking equipment that lets GPUs communicate. Its software coordinates the GPUs. Huang’s downfall It’s not clear when Jensen Huang started his affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a woman who U.S. intelligence officials reportedly suspect of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government has denied that she is a spy. Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a senior executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company that became an Nvidia customer. Megaspeed reportedly smuggled Nvidia’s chips into China , bypassing U.S. sanctions. The U.S. first restricted the export of Nvidia’s chips to China in 2022, citing the risk that China could use them for military development and to compete in AI. Alice Huang reportedly helped move $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips to China. The New York Times first reported on the relationship and the spy allegations on October 29 , and Jensen Huang initially said that it was an ordinary business relationship, not an affair. On November 6, the Financial Times reported that it was a romantic relationship . Two days later, Jensen Huang sent an email to Nvidia employees admitting that it had been an affair. On November 11, reports emerged that Huang also had an affair with one of his employees at Nvidia, reportedly Kimberly Powell , the company’s vice president of healthcare. On November 12, as pressure mounted from Nvidia’s board, Huang announced his resignation. Why Jensen Huang can’t easily be replaced It’s not simple for someone else to step into Huang’s shoes . He was directly involved in decisions that most executives would delegate, from managing in detail how Nvidia’s products were built to how salespeople talked to customers. A typical CEO might have five or 10 direct reports; Huang had as many as 60 direct reports. He reportedly sent hundreds of emails a…

articles.title: Google Pushes Privacy Angle As Gemini-Powered Smartglasses Debut
articles.content: Google is launching its first Gemini-powered smart glasses, with Samsung supplying the computing hardware. Given their built-in 12-megapixel camera, Google is emphasizing privacy protections, including a tamper-resistant recording light, automatic face redaction, and restrictions on real-time facial recognition and livestreaming. The company also promises not to use captured photos or videos for AI training or targeted advertising. Ars Technica reports: Google says the frames all weigh about 41 grams, which is not terrible but is definitely near the top for glasses generally. They will, naturally, weigh much more when you account for lenses. That will also determine the final pricing. So far, we only have the starting prices for these devices, including non-prescription lenses. The setup here is similar to the Ray-Ban Meta glasses we've seen for a few years. There are no screens in the lenses, but you can interact with the AI system via voice or by activating the integrated camera. The experience should be similar to using Gemini Live on your phone, but it will be a lot easier to fire up the AI. You can say "Hey Gemini" or tap a touch-sensitive area of the frame to start interacting with the robot. Since this is the same chatbot that operates across the Google ecosystem, it has access to your data and preferences. You can ask questions and get personalized answers, have Google Maps guide you by voice, or just talk with the AI to kill time. The glasses use custom open-ear speakers to limit distractions for those around you. Google notes the directional microphones should not pick up speech from other people, either. Adding the camera feed is where things get interesting. When the AI can see what you see, it has the potential to do more work on your behalf. Google suggests asking Gemini for recommendations when looking at a bookshelf or glancing at an event poster to have the AI add it to your calendar. The glasses will also support Gemini Guided Vision, which provides conversational audio descriptions for people who are visually impaired. The new frames are available for preorder today starting at $395. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Google faces calls for AI moratoriums in schools after Gemini pilot backlash
articles.content: CHICAGO—Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday, rallying against what they see as Google’s bid to entrench its AI models in schools, turn kids of all ages into Gemini guinea pigs, and hook them on AI. The backlash follows a Google statement last week, confirming that there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. While Google claimed it was giving schools “more choice, not less”—by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default—it would not provide an option that allowed Search without AI. For students, the only way to avoid interacting with AI was to remember to add “-ai” to every query, parents worried. In Chicago, many families showed up to protest Google, despite cold, rainy weather. Waving signs, dozens of protesters marched up to Google’s downtown office as workers seemed to be leaving for the day, shouting chants like “Hey Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini” and “Hey, Google, leave our kids alone!” Read full article Comments

articles.title: Palantir’s Karp takes a sharp left turn, says he and the company’s products are actually ‘progressive’
articles.content: With tech CEO roles, a certain level of shamelessness comes with the job description. Yet Alex Karp, head honcho of Palantir, seems set to raise the bar with a conspicuous display of political flexibility following the Democratic wave in the US midterms. In December 2024, Karp gave $1 million to the pro-Trump super PAC MAGA Inc . But it does not take cutting-edge AI and data analytics – in which Palantir claims to have unique power – for Karp to understand on which side his bread is buttered. The man with the distinctive verbal diarrhea is now stressing his progressive credentials – and those of Palantir's products. The CEO told Politico that he is now open to voting for the Democrats come 2028. "I've been a Democrat my whole life. I grew up in a far-left environment. I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet, and I absolutely believe Palantir – all of our products are essentially progressive," Karp reportedly said. Karp's explanation for his political generosity was an apparent desire for balance. "My giving is equal, Democrat, Republican," Karp told the publication. "I can tell you, without going into things I'm not gonna disclose, I'm very balanced, and everyone in the political arena knows it. And I'll tell you what, I'm also not the village idiot." All of which raises the question of whether, in avoiding idiocy, it is necessary to eschew any principled stance whatsoever. If only the Germans of the Weimar Republic had thought to fund both sides. Apparently, all Europe needed was a more balanced political donations portfolio. Such is Karp's sensitivity towards the topic that he once claimed: "I love when I'm getting yelled at in cities in Europe... Keep yelling at me... the only reason why someone's not goose-stepping between me and you is my product. Say thank you." They have not said thank you. In fact, across Europe, governments are looking to reject Palantir , while the EU has instigated a sovereign tech and AI policy to escape the clutches of the US tech giants. Karp has a talent for holding two seemingly contradictory positions. He has talked about the need for democratic societies to exercise hard power , and, elsewhere, about founding a company that could "power the West to its obvious innate superiority ." At the same time, he has presented Palantir as a force for peace. "We see ourselves as the pioneers of a genuine and viable antiwar movement ," he wrote in his shareholder letter. It is his company's association with a longstanding customer, the controversial US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), that has drawn the most criticism. In Minnesota earlier this year, federal immigration officers shot and killed two American citizens, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, in incidents captured on video. It has detained US citizens, and critics argue it has shown scant regard for due process. Karp denied that Palantir's association with ICE should reflect badly on the company. He told CNBC: " If you are critical of ICE, you should be out there protesting for more Palantir . Our product, actually, in its core, requires people to conform with Fourth Amendment data protection." In the Politico interview, Karp said he was "really happy to hear" President Trump, a driving force behind ICE's expansion, acknowledge after the midterm elections that ICE deportations have been too tough . "And I'm glad he's saying in public now what I've been saying in private," Karp told the news outlet. Karp has no shortage of public opinions on goose-stepping or innate Western superiority. Why, then, reserve his concerns about deportations for private conversations? A public intervention from a Trump donor and ICE supplier might have carried some weight. Maybe he doesn't care so long as people are still writing about Alex Karp. But anyone who cares about more than that might feel the need to take a hot shower and scrub off the associated trauma. ®

articles.title: Outlook, Microsoft 365, Teams and more down for thousands — live updates on massive outage
articles.content: Something is seriously wrong with Microsoft Outlook and other popular Microsoft services like Teams, Microsoft 365, Copilot and others, as more than 100,000 users are flocking to the popular outage-reporting website Downdetector to report issues. That number has dropped a bit since then, but it's still a very widespread outage. For its part, Microsoft has posted on X to its Microsoft 365 Status account about the issue and what it's doing to get things back in order. I eventually got the Microsoft 365 status page to load, and it's been keeping us updated on the latest issues. Microsoft Outlook outage — Live updates November 12, 2026 – 1:49 PM A massive number of reports (Image credit: Downdetector ) As of this post, Microsoft Outlook is sitting at more about 119,000 reports on Downdetector, which is a bit down from the peak of 130,000 but still a staggeringly large number of people having an issue with the productivity service. November 12, 2026 – 1:53 PM Microsoft is working on it While we're working to mitigate impact, we've confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region, more information will be provided in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543. November 12, 2026 Microsoft is aware of the issue and working on it. The company took to X to update users that it's "working to mitigate impact" and has "confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region." It didn't provide an updated time for when everything would be back to normal, but hopefully it can get things sorted quickly so emails and calendar alerts can start going again. November 12, 2026 – 1:56 PM That's a lot of Microsoft (Image credit: Downdetector ) While Outlook is getting the most attention in terms of raw reports, it's actually the whole of Microsoft 365 that's having problems, so other services are also experiencing outages that are impacting users, just not at the same scale as Outlook. November 12, 2026 – 2:00 PM The cause We've begun redistributing connection traffic across our broader worldwide infrastructure to help balance the load. More info under EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, as well as https://t.co/uFnnN6Svuf if the admin center is not available to you. November 12, 2026 Microsoft appears to have found the cause, as it posted on X saying that "We've determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors." It quickly followed up with another post saying, "We've begun redistributing connection traffic across our broader worldwide infrastructure to help balance the load." It sounds like the company might have a solution to the problem, though I have to assume that redistributing that much traffic will take some time, so it might be a while before everything is working flawlessly. November 12, 2026 – 2:02 PM Below 100,000 (Image credit: Downdetector ) Downdetector reports have dropped below 100,000 for Outlook, which likely means that some of Microsoft's traffic-redistribution methods are working for at least some percentage of users. November 12, 2026 – 2:08 PM Still can't access status page (Image credit: Shutterstock) While user reports are dropping, I personally still can't access the status page for Microsoft, so I'm forced to turn to X for the latest news (which isn't always as quick as going straight to the source). I've tried reloading the status page many times, and it's had the same result. Of course, we'll continue to monitor both the status page and X for the latest information. When the status page does start working again, that's probably a good sign. November 12, 2026 – 2:14 PM Status page loaded (Image credit: Microsoft) I decided to just leave the status page loading in the background without refreshing or anything. After about 5 minutes, I went back to the tab and saw that it finally loaded (probably took extra time due to…

articles.title: Nvidia’s interim CEO spent 13 years behind the scenes at Microsoft
articles.content: Colette Kress, Nvidia’s CFO since 2013, will keep that role while serving as interim CEO. (Nvidia Photo) Colette Kress, named Nvidia’s interim CEO on Thursday after Jensen Huang’s abrupt resignation, spent 13 years at Microsoft earlier in her career, including four as chief financial officer of the Redmond company’s Server and Tools business. But to say she was under the radar would be an understatement: a search of Seattle-area news archives turns up a single mention of her name from her Microsoft years, in a 2007 press release listing her as a presenter at a Hotel 1000 seminar on Microsoft’s budgeting software. Of course, that’s to be expected. Divisional finance execs aren’t typically public faces at Microsoft or anywhere else. But now she finds herself in the global spotlight, running the chipmaker at the center of the AI boom — at least for the time being. Nvidia announced Thursday that Huang resigned as president, CEO and a member of the board, effective immediately, following reports of an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials reportedly concluded was a Chinese spy, and a second affair with a direct report. Related Nvidia founder’s wife faces spotlight that MacKenzie Scott and Melinda French Gates know well Kress will remain CFO while the board searches for a permanent CEO, considering internal and external candidates. Director Harvey Jones, the former Synopsys CEO, becomes Nvidia’s first board chair. Nvidia shares fell more than 13% in early trading. Wall Street analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. wrote in a note Thursday morning that Kress has built “enormous credibility” inside and outside Nvidia. “We always believed she would eventually be CEO of a major public tech company, but she would have to leave Nvidia after many years there,” he wrote. Kress joined Microsoft in 1997 after finance roles at Texas Instruments, and held senior positions in corporate planning and finance before becoming chief financial officer of the Server and Tools business, which sold Windows Server, SQL Server and Visual Studio. Her LinkedIn profile lists her as a Microsoft corporate vice president from April 2006 to November 2010. Server and Tools was also a training ground for Microsoft’s current leadership. Satya Nadella took over the business in 2011, after Kress left, and used it as a springboard to the CEO job three years later. Amy Hood, now Microsoft’s CFO, served as its chief of staff earlier in her career. From Microsoft, Kress went to Cisco as senior vice president and CFO of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organization. Nvidia hired her as CFO in September 2013, ending a search of more than two years. Now as Nvidia’s interim CEO, her first major test comes quickly. Nvidia reports fiscal third-quarter results Tuesday, Nov. 17, with an earnings call scheduled for 2 p.m. Pacific.
articles.author: Todd Bishop
articles.fingerprint: behind ceo interim microsoft nvidia scenes spent years

articles.title: Optimizing cost per task and proving agent ROI on Amazon Bedrock
articles.content: Part 1 of this series built the operating model that controls Amazon Bedrock spend: attribution with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) principal tags and Cost and Usage Report 2.0, observability with model invocation logging, enforcement at three tiers, and a review cadence. That layer answers who spent it, and you can stop them. It can’t tell you whether the spend was well spent. This post answers two questions that Part 1 deliberately left open. First: Why is this workflow expensive? The answer requires thinking in cost per task, not cost per token. Second: Is the agent better than the humans were? The answer requires baselines, controlled experiments, and a scorecard tied to decisions. In this post, you learn a framework for calculating true model cost (including four hidden cost drivers that the pricing page doesn’t show), techniques for reducing cost per task through caching, routing, and output constraints, and a discipline for measuring agent ROI with human baselines, holdout experiments, and a five-dimension scorecard. This post is written for two audiences: the application and platform engineers who own the optimization levers, and the product owners and FinOps partners who need to justify agent spend to leadership. Cost per task, not cost per token Price per token invites quick comparison, but it doesn’t reflect what you actually pay. The published rate reflects the cost of a single token. Your bill reflects the cost of completing a task. A task is one complete unit of work your application asks a model to do: resolve one support email, extract fields from one invoice, or answer one user question. A task runs from the request through to a usable result, however many model calls it takes. The lower-priced model might not be the cheaper one to run. A cheaper model might fragment your text into more tokens, pad responses with filler, misread your tool schema and loop through corrections, or burn thousands of reasoning tokens before answering. None of these costs appear on the Bedrock pricing page . The four hidden cost drivers Four model characteristics determine what that published rate actually costs you on your workload. Tokenizer efficiency A token isn’t a word, and it is not equal across models. Every model family uses a different tokenizer and vocabulary. The same text, code, or JSON payload splits into different token counts. If Model A’s list price is 15 percent lower but its tokenizer needs 40 percent more tokens for your data (common with structured schemas and numerical arrays), Model B is cheaper. The gap widens for non-English text: many tokenizers fragment non-Latin scripts into two to three times more tokens than the equivalent English. Output alignment and verbosity Output tokens commonly cost 3–5x more than input tokens (the ratio varies by family. Refer to the Bedrock pricing page ). A model that ignores formatting constraints like “return only raw JSON” makes you pay that output premium for filler words. A model that follows formatting instructions closely saves money by generating fewer of these more expensive output tokens. Agentic loop efficiency Agentic workflows change the cost math entirely. Tool use (function calling) lets a model invoke external functions, requiring a multi-turn loop: analyze the prompt, decide to call a tool, wait for the observation, generate an answer. Each turn re-sends the full conversation history and tool results as input tokens. A model that takes four turns (each one re-sending a larger context payload) costs far more than one that finishes in a single pass. Reasoning overhead Many models support extended thinking , working through a chain of thought before the visible answer. Reasoning tokens bill as output tokens, so a model that thinks for 2,000 tokens before a 200-token answer bills you for 2,200. Some models redact the reasoning while still charging for it. Start with reasoning turned off and enable it only when benchmarks show a quality gap that…

articles.title: Building a self-service LLM gateway with Amazon Bedrock and LiteLLM
articles.content: Developers want AI coding assistants with minimal setup. With a large language model (LLM) gateway and LiteLLM, they can quickly access foundation models (FMs) available on Amazon Bedrock while you gain visibility and usage control. Platform teams need to monitor latency and errors, finance teams need to attribute inference costs to teams and projects, and security teams need consistent access controls. An LLM gateway can help address these needs by providing a centrally managed access point to the models that power coding assistants. In this post, we show how to build a self-service LLM gateway using Amazon Bedrock Application Inference Profiles with LiteLLM running on AWS Fargate to abstract Amazon Bedrock behind an OpenAI-compatible API. With this pattern, developers can access foundation models through a single API with a dedicated key while you gain per-user cost controls and model performance observability. By the end, you will understand the pattern well enough to build your own version from the illustrative snippets and AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) constructs. This post uses Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku models for example purposes. For a list of models and availability by AWS Region, see Supported models by AWS Region in Amazon Bedrock . This LLM gateway pattern follows a straightforward request flow from the developer, through the LiteLLM layer, to Amazon Bedrock and the underlying FM. The following diagram illustrates the production topology behind that flow. For simplicity, we don’t cover the addition of Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, such as content filtering and grounding, but you would normally include appropriate responsible AI controls before deploying to production. A developer’s OpenAI-compatible client reaches the LLM gateway through Amazon Route 53, Amazon CloudFront, and an Application Load Balancer (ALB). It authenticates to LiteLLM on Fargate with a per-user API key. Behind that, the request draws on Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) (PostgreSQL) for virtual-key and spend state. It also interacts with Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey as a cache, and AWS Secrets Manager for secrets. LiteLLM then ultimately invokes Amazon Bedrock Application Inference Profiles using a scoped AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) task role. Amazon CloudWatch captures requests per minute (RPM) and tokens per minute (TPM) metrics and the quota alarm. Figure 1: LLM gateway architecture (production topology) The architecture consists of these core components: LiteLLM on AWS Fargate : LiteLLM provides a proxy that exposes an OpenAI-compatible API. We run it on an AWS Fargate task with target-tracking Auto Scaling on CPU utilization. Developers point their tools at this endpoint and don’t interact with Amazon Bedrock directly. Self-service portal : LiteLLM includes a lightweight portal for admin and developer self-service. This web app can integrate with your corporate single sign-on (SSO). Using the portal, operations engineers set the spend policy while developers self-provision API keys within those parameters. Persistent and cache storage : LiteLLM uses Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey for non-persistent response caching. It also coordinates rate-limiting across AWS Fargate tasks. A separate Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL) database is the database of record for persistent state such as API key metadata and spend tracking. Amazon Bedrock Application Inference Profiles : Each model (such as Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku) gets its own inference profile, which you manage using the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK). With this, you get per-model quota isolation and a clean abstraction layer between LiteLLM’s configuration and the model versioning of Amazon Bedrock. Langfuse : Open source LLM observability for prompt-level telemetry, latency tracking, and debugging. It complements the infrastructure-level metrics of Amazon CloudWatch with application-level insight. By using an OpenAI-compatible protocol, developers can…

articles.title: Netflix releases new trailer for Ray Gunn
articles.content: We caught the first trailer for the upcoming Netflix animated film Ray Gunn in September and were charmed by director Brad Bird's blend of a Jetsons-like future with classic 1930s noir detective thrillers. Bird has described it as a mashup of The Maltese Falcon and Buck Rogers , and the latest trailer definitely gives off that energy. As previously reported , Bird has directed some of our all-time favorite animated films: The Iron Giant (1999), The Incredibles (2004), and Ratatouille (2007), with the latter two snagging well-deserved Oscar wins. He's been kicking around the idea for Ray Gunn for the last 30 years, working on his many other film projects while the Ray Gunn script—co-written by Matthew Robbins, who also co-wrote 1987’s Batteries Not Included with Bird—“stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers,” the director said earlier this year. The film’s inspiration came when Bird heard the opening of the B-52s’ “ Planet Claire ” (a personal favorite that also provides the soundtrack to the new trailer) and initially thought it was a cover of Henry Mancini’s theme music from the classic TV show Peter Gunn . Bird is a longtime fan of film noir and hard-boiled detectives, and he came up with the idea of a futuristic detective named Ray Gunn (a play on " raygun ," of course). “It’s film noir and a hard-boiled detective story, but it’s got a lot more comedy and a lot more action than the average film noir,” said Bird . articles.title: New OnePlus update gives phones and tablets the ability to auto-unlock PCs
articles.content: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority TL;DR OnePlus is rolling out a new OxygenOS 16 update for phones and tablets. The update introduces the ability to automatically unlock your PC with your mobile device. The rollout is expected to reach all users around November 19, 2026. It would be nice if phones and PCs had more cross-device functionality than they currently have. Microsoft has been working toward that goal, releasing features like a Mobile devices tile that lets users toggle Do Not Disturb mode, adjust the phone’s volume, or make it play a sound when misplaced. But Microsoft isn’t the only company trying to bring PCs and phones closer together. OnePlus is rolling out a new feature that would be very convenient for PC users. This week, OnePlus announced the rollout of its November update. Phones will be getting version C20P01(BRB1EX01), while tablets will receive version C20P01(BRB3EX01). For OxygenOS 16 devices, this update will introduce the ability to automatically unlock your PC with your mobile device.
articles.author: Ryan McNeal

articles.title: Building a rocket is hard. AST SpaceMobile thinks it's "simple."
articles.content: During an hour-long event on Thursday, Abel Avellan, the founder and chief executive of the telecommunications company AST SpaceMobile, laid out his vision for developing a large rocket to launch his Bluebird satellites into orbit. Avellan emphasized, over and over again, that AST plans to build a "simple" rocket. He paraphrased SpaceX founder Elon Musk several times, saying, "the best part is no part." Avellan emphasized that AST has already procured engines for its proposed Blacklift rocket, asserting that engine development accounts for 80 percent of a typical rocket's development cycle. "Of course rocket engineers are going to get mad with me, but you can simplify it as a big tank feeding engines," he said of the rocket. "So big tanks—we know how to do them. We know how to do them. We know how to do them in composite." Read full article Comments
articles.author: Eric Berger

articles.title: Man's secret use of synthetic testosterone for cows nearly destroyed his heart
articles.content: For 11 years, a Massachusetts man had an alarming array of health problems, most notably that his heart kept failing. He landed in the hospital over and over again, needed life support at one point, spent years going to specialists, and underwent a barrage of tests along the way. But through it all, he never revealed a key detail behind his ailments: He was taking powerful, illicit synthetic testosterone derivatives (aka anabolic-androgenic steroids, or AAS). One of the drugs he took was approved only for use in animals; it's primarily used to beef up cows. Left in the dark, his doctors had to puzzle this out on their own. In a case report in this week's issue of the New England Journal of Medicine, they explain how they did it. They also offer a warning: These cases will only become more common, and clinicians need to know what they look like. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Software Samaritan revamps borked Indian certs to block smart TV ads
articles.content: eMudhra's private key exposure has been a security disaster, but it also means that you can block those annoying ads on smart TVs if you’re so inclined. Luckily for those with some know-how and a hatred of smart TV ads, Czech software developer Daniel Vrátil has done the work for you and published his project on GitHub for anyone who wants to take a stab at it - and do the legwork to add support for their own ad-riddled television. Vrátil said he’d been blocking ads on his Samsung smart TV using a Pi-hole (DNS-based ad-blocking software that can run on a Raspberry Pi, for those unfamiliar), but right around the time the eMudhra certificate leak mess unfolded, he had messed something up while tinkering with his home lab and the ads were back. First, here's a bit of background on the eMudhra mess. The company, based in India, operated a publicly trusted HTTPS certificate authority and says it has issued more than 60 million digital certificates. As we learned last month , eMudhra wasn't doing its best to keep its cryptographic keys safe: Eight intermediate CA private keys were found to be absurdly weak, with one being the number four and the others consisting of two- or three-digit numbers that could be guessed with little effort. eMudhra has since left the CA racket , saying that it wasn’t a big deal to it since issuing certs was a small part of its business. The company has blamed a bad software script put in place to generate keys that its hardware couldn’t handle as the root of the issue. What all that means, in a practical sense, is that anyone could forge an eMudhra certificate to spoof a website and do something malicious. It also means that security researchers who were able to get their hands on devices that still trust eMudhra certificates could have a field day learning how their communications work, which is exactly what Vrátil took advantage of. eMudhra private keys were added to the open source mitmproxy service - a fully interactive HTTPS proxy that can be used for good or bad - shortly after they were exposed. Pair that with a 2022 Samsung smart TV that still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates, and you have a way to inspect its HTTPS traffic and redirect selected requests to a server of your choosing. By Vrátil’s account, swapping out annoying ads for pictures of his family on his TV’s main screen was a pretty simple task. “Luckily for me, Samsung did not yet release an update for my TV that would revoke the certificate,” Vrátil explained in his writeup. “This allowed me to route all traffic from the TV through mitmproxy and get a list of all the domains and endpoints that my TV talks to, but also see the structure of the requests and response payloads.” The advertising traffic flow was pretty basic, it turns out: Activity on the TV is relayed to an ad server, which serves up ads on the home screen based on a JSON response. By generating a certificate for Samsung's advertising domains using a compromised eMudhra signing key, and configuring his router to direct requests for those domains to a server on his home network, Vrátil was able to replace ads with family photos served from his NAS. He also added code that tosses other requests to those advertising domains, including tracking data, into a black hole rather than forwarding them to Samsung's servers. As mentioned above, it’s on GitHub for those who want to trick their TV, if it still supports eMudhra certificates, but you’ll have to do the legwork to dissect how your device is getting ads and tweak the code to work. “It's not exactly a one-click setup,” Vrátil told The Register in an email. He’s invited people to try it out, but no one has bothered to submit a pull request to add support for their own device to his public repo. It’s also worth noting that this is only going to work as long as vulnerable devices keep trusting eMudhra certificates, which hopefully means you need to act fast. That said, smart TVs that are out of support may never…

articles.title: Iconic First Image of Black Hole Holds Up To Scrutiny
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from The Conversation: On April 10 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) Collaboration revealed the first picture of a black hole. The object is at the centre of a galaxy known as M87, about 55 million light-years away. The iconic ring structure instantly became one of the most recognized scientific images of the modern era. It showed a black hole "shadow" outlined by light from swirling hot gas -- just as predicted by Einstein's theory of general relativity. The result supported the long-standing idea that the centers of galaxies house supermassive black holes. However, scientists have since had some disagreements on whether the details and structure of the ring in the original publication were accurate. Our new research, published today in Nature, used new techniques to investigate the original datasets. Not only do our results validate the original work, but they also provide a fresh perspective on the ring structure. Our independent results enhance confidence in one of the most significant modern scientific results. And we bring the image of a black hole millions of light-years away back into focus. [...] When compared directly to images from the EHT collaboration, our result is consistent in diameter and overall orientation. Naturally, there are some differences in the fine details of ring width and surface brightness along the circumference, but the overall structure matches. This provides a fresh perspective on the iconic black hole ring while also resolving previous discrepancies. To prove this success didn't depend solely on advanced machine learning, we also developed a complementary imaging method based on traditional statistical techniques. This entirely different method also validated our structure using the new closure invariant data we produced. Overall, our work delivers a strong independent validation of the supermassive black hole structure at the centre of galaxy M87. And it could do more in the future. Our technique could also be useful in other situations where data from multiple sensors are combined to map unknown structures -- such as medical imaging or mapping earthquakes. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Run agents securely and efficiently with the next generation AgentCore runtime
articles.content: AI agents have moved past one-off prompts. They now run multi-step workloads for hours at a time. The length of task that frontier agents can complete on their own doubles about every four months ( METR ), and 40 percent of large enterprises are scaling AI agents, up from 27 percent a year ago ( McKinsey ). As agents run longer and with more autonomy, the focus shifts from what agents can do to how securely, reliably, and economically they can operate at scale. Agents do more than traditional software: they execute code, navigate browsers, access sensitive data, and act on behalf of users. These capabilities introduce new security and infrastructure demands, making strong isolation essential for production deployments. Every agent session needs a secure, isolated environment. But delivering that isolation at scale introduces a fundamental challenge: balancing performance, cost, and efficiency. Pre-provisioned environments consume resources even when idle, driving up costs. On-demand environments reduce wasted capacity but introduce cold-start latency, delaying agent execution. Neither approach scales efficiently without trade-offs. As organizations move from deploying a handful of agents to running thousands of concurrent sessions, building and managing custom sandboxes becomes increasingly complex, expensive, and unpredictable. The challenge is evident. Only 15 percent of organizations have scaled orchestrated, multi-agent systems, and 70 percent say they can’t yet trust and govern their agents ( Deloitte ). Scaling agents shouldn’t mean choosing between security, speed, and cost. The next generation of agent infrastructure must deliver strong isolation with fast startup times, elastic scaling, and usage-based economics. Because as AI agents move into production, secure execution shouldn’t be the bottleneck. It should be the foundation that makes scale possible. The fastest path to production should also be the safest one. The next generation AgentCore runtime We built Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to help developers build, connect, and optimize agents securely at scale. AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, is the managed compute layer. It gives developers a fully managed environment to deploy and run agents without building or maintaining infrastructure. Since launching, our customers have been pushing their agents into increasingly complex workloads. As those workloads grow, so do the demands on the execution environment: more compute, more flexible billing, and trust boundaries that extend to data, not only compute. Agents reach production at scale if the infrastructure underneath was built for both scale and speed. Today we’re announcing updates to AgentCore runtime that meet those demands. The core guarantee stands: every session runs in its own hardware-isolated Firecracker micro virtual machine (MicroVM), with its own identity, policy, and audit trail. These updates expand what’s possible within that guarantee. Sessions now start up to 15x faster, scale to 4x more compute, and run up to 68% more efficiently, with the isolation boundary fully intact. Here’s what’s new. Run bigger workloads without waiting longer to start Teams building increasingly advanced agents asked for more flexibility: the ability to scale memory and compute within the isolated session to match the demands of their workloads. From large codebase compilations to browser-driven workflows to local model inference, the execution environment needs to keep pace. Sessions now scale 4x compared to the previous version, up to 8 vCPUs and 32 GB, with support for container images up to 10 GB. Sessions start in under 2 seconds, independent of image size and concurrency. You no longer need warm pools and pre-provisioned clusters to manage cold starts. “Migrating to the next generation of AgentCore runtime reduced our agent session cold starts from nearly a minute to under five seconds, even during peak traffic. It also eliminated startup…

articles.title: Nvidia only the latest to look towards Apple for salvation
articles.content: Whether you're in processors, entertainment, or cars, if your firm is tanking, all you'll hear is that Apple should step in, either with employees or a straight buyout offer. Even though it never does. Jensen Huang is out as Nvidia CEO and immediately analysts are saying Apple staffers should replace him. Just as they keep saying Apple should buy Disney. Images credit: Huang (Nvidia), Disneyworld (Disney). There was about a day between Nvidia's board meeting to oust CEO Jensen Huang and his resigning . You can guess what conversations were going on there, but you could also predict one thing about the world's reaction. Before Huang even knew he was out, there were reports that he will be replaced by Apple's Johny Srouji . Those reports said Srouji was being considered and pointedly did not say whether Srouji had even been asked yet. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

articles.title: Nvidia founder’s wife faces spotlight that MacKenzie Scott and Melinda French Gates know well
articles.content: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang during a Microsoft Windows and Surface event in San Francisco on Oct. 7. (Ken Yeung Photo for GeekWire) As the fallout from Jensen Huang’s affair came to a head with his resignation as Nvidia CEO on Thursday, attention has turned in part to his wife, Lori Huang, who has stayed largely in the background during their 41-year marriage. A New York Times profile , and other media coverage, placed Lori Huang alongside two familiar Seattle names — MacKenzie Scott, ex-wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, and Melinda French Gates, ex-wife of Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates — as tech billionaires’ spouses who have faced infidelity playing out in public. Huang acknowledged to employees on Sunday that he had been unfaithful to his wife. The admission followed Times reporting last month that a Chinese businesswoman he had become close to had been identified by U.S. officials as an intelligence asset. China has denied the espionage claims. On Wednesday, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, citing five people who worked at the company. Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO. Kress spent 13 years at Microsoft earlier in her career. Huang was worth about $145 billion as of Wednesday’s close, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index , nearly all of it from his roughly 3.4% stake in Nvidia. That figure doesn’t reflect Thursday’s drop: Nvidia shares fell more than 13% at the open, pushing the company’s market value below $4 trillion, CNBC reported . Huang’s fortune peaked at as much as $195 billion in May, according to Bloomberg. More than half of his 922 million shares belong to a trust where he and Lori Huang are co-trustees, the Times reported, and she solely controls a separate trust holding about $5 billion in Nvidia stock. Scott and French Gates each came out of their divorces with vast fortunes. Scott, whose split from Bezos was announced in 2019 , left with about $38 billion. French Gates, who divorced Gates in 2021 , received an estimated $25 billion in a settlement that was never publicly disclosed, The Independent reported . Both have since steered billions into philanthropy. Scott has donated $26 billion through her organization, Yield Giving. French Gates left the Gates Foundation in 2024 with $12.5 billion for her own work. George Rush, who co-wrote the Daily News gossip column Rush & Molloy, told the Times that the Huang situation differs from the Bezos and Gates splits in one key way: this relationship has the potential to move markets and carry global consequences. A copy of the Jan. 28, 2019, edition of the National Enquirer featuring Jeff Bezos . (GeekWire Photo) There has been no report of any plans by the Huangs to separate. Lori Huang did not respond to the Times’ request for comment. In his message to employees, Huang asked for privacy for his family, saying they bear no responsibility for his choices. The couple’s story has Pacific Northwest roots. Jensen Huang, born in Taiwan, was sent as a child to live with relatives in Tacoma, Wash., and later went to high school in Beaverton, Ore., according to Quartr . Lori Huang also graduated from an Oregon high school. The two met in the early 1980s at Oregon State University, where Lori Huang, then Lori Mills, was one of only a handful of women studying engineering, the Times reported. They were paired as lab partners in an electrical engineering fundamentals class, and Huang later told OSU that meeting her was “the most important, single event of OSU, and of my life.” After graduating and marrying, the Huangs moved to Silicon Valley to work as chip designers. Lori Huang worked at Silicon Graphics, where she earned more than her husband did at LSI Logic, he told The New Yorker in 2023 . Just before Nvidia’s founding in 1993, she gave up her career to raise their two children, Spencer and Madison, who both now work at Nvidia. Huang has frequently credited her support.…

articles.title: ‘Water for life, not data’: Amazon data center plan draws Eastern Washington protests
articles.content: Inside an Amazon data center. (AWS Photo / Noah Berger) Amazon’s plans to build a data center campus near the Columbia River in Eastern Washington drew pushback Monday at a meeting of the Walla Walla County commissioners. Some attendees held handmade and printed signs reading “Amazon lies,” “Big tech is shady. No more data centers” and “Water for life, not data,” according to the Walla Walla Union-Bulletin and its photos of the event. The majority of the roughly 56 public comments were opposed to or had concerns about data center development, including worries about groundwater supplies, effects on agriculture and wildlife, and a lack of transparency, the Union-Bulletin reported. Supporters pointed to potential benefits from job creation and economic development. Related Data center developers brace for new reality as election backlash sinks in The meeting highlighted continued resistance to data centers from communities concerned about higher electricity bills, depleted freshwater supplies and other environmental and social repercussions. Over the past year, tech giants including Amazon and Microsoft have pledged to limit those impacts and invest in host communities, but those commitments have not ended the opposition. Elected officials are increasingly considering legislation and local ordinances to set standards and require greater transparency — an approach some tech leaders say could help address public concerns. “There is a role for good laws, and if laws emerge that require that everybody do this work in a responsible way, I think that might be part of the solution,” Brad Smith, Microsoft vice chair and president, recently told reporters at a company event . Commissioners in Western Washington’s Skagit County last month adopted significant restrictions on data center development. The facilities are prohibited in unincorporated areas, with some exceptions, and new caps on size and electricity usage will limit the technology to small-scale operations. Amazon’s data center expansion in Washington The planned Walla Walla County campus is one of two projects that would mark Amazon’s first large-scale data center developments in its home state. The second is in West Richland, part of the Tri-Cities. Amazon already operates smaller data centers in Washington. The Walla Walla County campus would occupy roughly 134 acres at Wallula Gap Business Park, on property formerly owned by the Port of Walla Walla. Its three proposed single-story data center buildings would create about 120 to 150 full-time jobs, Amazon said. According to a company fact sheet, the campus would use roughly 14 million gallons of water from the public utility to cool its equipment during its first year of operation. Amazon says it is working with the port to build a system that would replace the utility-supplied cooling water with nonpotable water drawn from the Columbia River. Wastewater from the campus “will meet industrial reuse standards,” the company said. The campus would also use about 6 million gallons of utility-supplied water annually for employee needs. Amazon’s fact sheet says the company will cover the electricity costs associated with the data center and that the “expenses aren’t added to the bills of local residents or businesses.” The company is also working with partners to develop a nuclear power plant using small modular nuclear reactors near the Tri-Cities. The proposed plant could begin operating in the 2030s and “will provide net-new carbon-free energy for communities in the Pacific Northwest, including Eastern Washington,” Amazon said. Despite Amazon’s assurances, many attendees at Monday’s meeting called for a one-year, countywide moratorium on new data center development, the Union-Bulletin reported. Commissioner Bertha Clayton said she would consider a pause on new applications to give officials time to draft an ordinance to better regulate the developments. Clayton said zoning changes adopted now would be…

articles.title: Save $119 on DDR5 RAM with this high-end AM5 gaming combo from Newegg
articles.content: Newegg has refreshed its bundle deals and have recently come out with a couple of solid deals that help take some of the sting out of building a PC in these trying times. The latest combo pairs one of the fastest gaming CPUs in the Ryzen 5 9800X3D, 32GB of Corsair DDR5-6000 RAM, and a premium motherboard with MSI’s X870E Carbon Wifi for only $1,250.98 , saving $119 compared to buying the parts individually. In fact, buying this RAM kit alone would cost $509.99, so if you apply the discount to the RAM, it’s just $390 and cheaper than any comparable standalone kit, which looks to be around $460 at the time of this writing. Newegg also throws in a free Rosewill 360mm AIO ($90 value) to sweeten the pot. Check out all the RAM Combo deals at Newegg The RAM portion of the bundle, Corsair’s Vengeance RGB 32GB (2x16GB) DDR5-6000 CL36 RAM kit, is currently available on Newegg for an eye-watering $509.99 when bought separately. The good news is that the discount brings this RAM down to something reasonable for the times. This black kit matches the MSI X870E Carbon board in the combo and features a frosted RGB light bar that runs the length of the sticks. If RGB lighting isn’t your thing and you prefer a stealthy, unassuming look, you can turn it off. The DDR5-6000 speed lands in the sweet spot for the AM5 platform and is a worthwhile, good-looking option. The SK Hynix ICs under the heatsink pair nicely with the MSI board and offer plenty of overclocking headroom. free rosewill frostmax 360mm aio ($90 value) Ryzen 5 9800X3D, 32GB Crosair DDR5-6000 RAM, MSI X870E Carbon Wifi Motherboard: was $1369.97 now $1250.98 Save $119 on this 3-item Newegg combo that includes 32GB of Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 CL36 RAM, the awesome-for-gaming Ryzen 5 9800X3D CPU, and a premium motherboard with MSI's X870E Carbon Wifi. View Deal Next is one of the most popular and fastest current-generation gaming CPUs: the Ryzen 7 9800X3D . This 8-core/16-thread Zen5-based processor has a 4.6 GHz base clock and a 5.2 GHz max boost, plenty fast for any task. The X3D variant's 96MB of L3 cache helps with gaming (among other things), making it one of the fastest gaming CPUs available . It is also a well-rounded performer that excels in games and suits most applications. Last but certainly not least is the premium MSI X870E Carbon Wifi motherboard (one we reviewed in the past. We loved the robust power delivery (perfect for the 9800X3D or greater), the dual Ethernet ports, EZ features, storage options (4x SATA, 4x M.2 sockets - one PCie 5.0) and ample connectivity on the rear I/O, including four USB Type-C ports (2x 40 Gbps). The all-black motherboard sports a cool RGB design element of the MSI dragon on the VRM heatsink to break up the monotony and lend some bling to the inside of your chassis. It’s a great motherboard to build your AM5 rig around. In the end, we like this combo as this, and others like it, help take some of the pain out of buying a PC today. Priced at $1,250.98 with a savings of $118.99 and a free 360mm Rosewill Frostmax Digital ARGB AIO ($90 value), it’s one of the better bundles available on Newegg right now. Get it while supplies last.

articles.content: AWS has released AWS Emulator , a local emulator of the AWS APIs. You run it on a laptop, a dev server or in CI. The AWS CLI and SDKs talk to it instead of AWS. No AWS account is needed, and there is no service fee . The unusual part: autonomous agents wrote and reviewed all of its code . For developers and coding agents, AWS Emulator gives a fast, free test loop against AWS-shaped APIs. TL;DR Size: Built from 438 AWS API models , covering 200+ services . One Rust crate per service. Runs on: Linux x86_64/aarch64 (RPM or Debian), or Docker on macOS/Windows with a 2 GiB memory limit. Source builds need 100 GB of free disk. Performance: Passes 24,243 of 42,857 scored fidelity tests (56.6%) in release v1.0.322 . Best: AWS KMS at 93.9% (291 of 310 tests); Amazon SQS at 89.8%. Worst: AWS CloudFormation at 15.8% (414 of 2,612 tests). What is AWS Emulator? AWS Emulator is a headless local program from AWS that serves an AWS API endpoint. You point the CLI or an SDK at it with environment variables. Your code does not change. Resources live in memory and vanish when it stops. The docs show a DynamoDB example. A CreateTable call with a 2-character name fails with the same ValidationException text AWS returns. How did AI agents build AWS Emulator? The project began with a prompt to Kiro . It returned a passable Amazon SQS emulator in about 15 minutes. AWS then split the work across 3 teams of agents: Test writers derive scenarios from the public Smithy API models and verify each against real AWS. Issue finders replay those tests against the emulator and file failures. Fixers take 1 issue each and submit a patch. Every patch passes a merge gate covering build, code review, security and fidelity. Several security agents run adversarial reviews . Matthew Goldberg reports hundreds of concurrent agents fixing thousands of issues a day. The release pipeline runs on AWS Developer Tools, with CodeCommit as the agents’ repository. Code reaches GitHub last. How accurate is AWS Emulator? AWS publishes a scores.json file with each release. We tallied the v1.0.322 file , scored on November 11, 2026. Overall: 24,243 of 42,857 scored tests pass (56.6%); 80 were skipped. Step level: 49,810 of 68,007 individual steps pass (73.2%). Cross-service workflows: 2,752 of 6,569 pass (41.9%). Core services: S3 79.1%, DynamoDB 77.3%, SNS 73.9%, Lambda 46.4%, EC2 41.5%. Per the fidelity docs , control-plane APIs match AWS best. Data-plane, CloudFormation, Terraform and CDK support varies by service. Unimplemented operations return HTTP 501 NotImplemented . The tests live in aws-emulator-evaluation-suite , including failing ones. How do you run AWS Emulator? There are 4 paths, per the README : Linux: install the RPM or Debian package and run aws-emulator . macOS/Windows: build a container from AWS’s Dockerfile , capped at 2 GiB memory. Rust embedded mode: add it as a dev-dependency for 1 isolated instance per test. Coding agents: aws agent-toolkit add-skill --skill-name aws-emulator , with AWS CLI 2.35.0 or later. A source build serves HTTPS on 127.0.0.1:9297 with a self-signed certificate. It needs a Rust toolchain, a C compiler and at least 100 GB of disk. Embedded mode carries the same build cost on the first cargo test . How does it compare with LocalStack, Moto and Floci? articles.title: New AAPL $425 target bets big on unproven iPhone Duo supercycle
articles.content: China Renaissance has raised its Apple price target by over 50% to $425, betting that the iPhone Duo will spark a major upgrade cycle despite limited evidence that early demand will translate into sustained sales. iPhone Duo The Chinese financial services firm upgraded Apple from Hold to Buy on November 11, reversing a downgrade issued just 99 days earlier. China Renaissance previously cited rising component costs and slowing services growth as reasons for its more cautious outlook. Analysts Jack Zhou and Lemuel Lin now believe Apple's first foldable iPhone could become a major source of growth. They expect the iPhone Duo to change how customers use their iPhones and potentially encourage earlier upgrades. China Renaissance sees the iPhone Duo as an opportunity to drive growth over the coming decade, outweighing the financial pressures that prompted its earlier downgrade. articles.title: Constellation Space launches its platform for managing fleets of satellites with AI tools
articles.content: Constellation Space’s software platform uses machine learning to optimize satellite data transfer. (Constellation Space Illustration) Seattle-based Constellation Space is rolling out its flagship software platform, which uses machine learning to streamline operations for fleets of satellites and the ground networks that serve them. “We build models in-house for things like weather, attenuation, signal jamming, demand … and synthesize all of that to help operators understand what their ground contact plan looks like in the future, and how to optimize their fleets,” CEO Kamran Majid told GeekWire. The Constellation Platform is tailor-made for a growing number of satellite constellations in low Earth orbit. Keeping track of thousands of satellites — and the best opportunities for downlinking data from each of those satellites — is becoming an increasingly complicated task. Constellation Space, which was founded last year , draws upon Majid’s experience as a NASA engineering intern and as a software engineer working on SpaceX’s Starlink satellite network. “At Starlink, I saw firsthand how manual mission-control processes break down as constellations scale,” he said. “I started Constellation to help smaller teams get ahead of link failures instead of spending their time rebuilding pass plans and recovering from outages.” A video produced by Constellation Space features its operations platform for satellite fleets. Majid’s fellow co-founders include chief technology officer Raaid Kabir , a veteran of Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin space venture, and Omeed Tehrani and Laith Altarabishi , who were previously software engineers at Capital One. “We’re a team of six people right now,” Majid said. One year into its existence, Constellation Space has already gained traction. Several months ago, the startup said it raised $7.5 million in a seed round backed by Y Combinator, Nvidia, OpenAI, Samsung Next and other investors. Majid said an early version of the Constellation Platform has attracted more than 10 customers, including Amazon Web Services. It’s also used by more than 20 academic institutions. “Our annual contract value this year is $2.25 million,” he said. The platform combines forecasts for factors affecting satellite transmissions — including space situational awareness, weather conditions, signal-to-noise ratios, signal jamming and bandwidth demand — to predict how many gigabytes of data can be transmitted during a given pass. Operators can then use that data to optimize transmission settings and schedules. Its machine-learning model is pre-trained on data from a global network of sensors. Once it’s deployed, the model adapts to each fleet’s specific hardware and ground stations. Constellation Space says satellite operators can boost downlinked data per pass by as much as 36%. Majid said the journey from SpaceX to startup has been “really interesting.” Constellation Space CEO Kamran Majid (Constellation Space Photo) “The mindset is very similar,” he said. “I was previously an engineer. Now I’m finding myself in more of a business role. The mindset is just ‘first-principles thinking’ about everything. Eliminate all the requirements that don’t make sense before you even start to think about solving the problem. Those core tenets have stayed as we’ve progressed as a venture, and I think that’s been really important to our success so far.” Setting up the startup in the Seattle area, where more than half of the world’s satellites are built , has also been interesting. “We are a Y Combinator company , so we were in San Francisco for a couple of months, and there was a lot of pressure from the community in SF to have everyone be in San Francisco. We definitely felt that a little bit,” Majid said. “But operating in the satellite…
