articles.title: Spotify’s AI DJ just got 9 new voices and you can finally reduce their chatter — here’s how this new update works
articles.content: Spotify’s foray into the world of AI has resulted in the introduction of the “AI DJ” feature, which acts as a personalized guide that helps curate the music you listen to and even talks to you about whatever you’re currently jamming to. This exclusive Spotify Premium subscriber feature has emerged as a fun way to prompt and speak to your personal AI DJ and request tunes based on your mood, what specific genres you want to hear, the type of activities you want a playlist for and more. Thanks to the power of OpenAI’s generative AI technology and Sonantic’s AI voice capabilities, Spotify’s AI DJ feature is possible. Alongside English, the AI DJ can also speak to users in Spanish, French, German, Italian and Brazilian Portuguese. Now that same feature has expanded to include even more voices that match varied personalities, plus you can even decrease the rate at which they speak to you. Here’s how it works. New voices, new personalities and a new toggle feature that makes them talk less (Image credit: Shutterstock) Right now, Spotify Premium users can select from a new collection of AI DJ voices that speak in either English or Spanish. Seven new English voice options have been added to cover American, British, Irish, Australian and Indian accents, while the two other voices speak primarily in Spanish. Accessing these new AI DJ voices is as easy as opening the app, using the search tool to find “DJ,” tapping the three-dot menu and choosing your AI DJ’S voice & commentary settings from there. Here’s the full lineup of all the new Spotify AI DJ’s you can interact with: Casey [US]: Laidback energy, warm, bit of a drawl. Tess [US]: Direct but inviting, has a bit of an edge. In-the-know. Lane [US]: Southern accent, brings a younger, positive energy. Sam [AU]: Gregarious, fun, likes to keep things not-so-serious. Nell [UK]: Mellow, slower energy, and deeply knowledgeable. Declan [IR]: Straightforward, passionate, and a bit of a music nerd. Nisha [IN]: Inviting, with contagious energy. Nico [MX]: Down to earth, present, and right there with you. Fabi [MX]: Witty, friendly, and always a step ahead. If you’d prefer your AI DJ not to talk as much between songs, Spotify has now given you the option to make that happen. A new toggle has been added that will keep your AI DJ from interrupting your music streaming sessions as it once did and let your playlist flow more seamlessly. Bottom line Spotify has done a lot to improve its user experience via AI. Alongside the AI DJ feature, the streaming service has introduced the “Taste Profile” music & podcast recommendation tool, AI-powered “Prompted Playlists” and the ability to create playlists within ChatGPT thanks to the streaming service's official plugin. Having a new array of voices and personalities to choose from within Spotify’s AI DJ ecosystem is pretty cool, as it widens its appeal to more nationalities and tastes in personalities. Here’s hoping even more languages get added to the AI DJ feature over time to increase its international reach even further. articles.title: Chainguard defends its choice to break the PHP security embargo: “We own the decision.”
articles.content: At KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 this week , Chainguard co-founder and CTO Matt Moore defended the company’s decision to release patched PHP images before an agreed-upon embargo with other partners had lifted. When Chainguard shipped patched PHP container images more than six hours ahead of an October 21 coordinated security release, PHP’s maintainers accused the company of giving attackers a head start. Chainguard argues attackers already had one. Chainguard founder and CTO Matt Moore In an interview with The New Stack , Moore said, “We own the decision that we chose to do it. Nobody could force us to do it — but we did not do it in a vacuum.” He also described, in discussions with TNS, other participants in the embargo and security vendors’ reports of activity targeting the vulnerabilities before Chainguard released its images. Chainguard was not saying that they patched it faster so they shipped it first. According to Moore, Chainguard believed attackers could already exploit the bugs, or were at least close to figuring out how — or were trying to figure it out. The two vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 (out-of-memory corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (stale global state) , collectively known as PHP2Shell, were serious memory-management and error-handling flaws. Under the right conditions, an unauthenticated attacker could execute code on a PHP server. The two bugs involved PHP’s handling of memory exhaustion and its failure to clear references to freed memory between requests. In the first, reaching a memory limit at the wrong moment could interrupt PHP before it finished setting up internal data. Later processing could mistake that unfinished data for valid information. In the second vulnerability, an error could leave PHP holding a reference to memory from an earlier request that had already been freed. A subsequent request could then access that invalid memory. Under exploitable conditions, these failures could let an attacker run code inside the server’s PHP process. Researchers demonstrated remote code execution through both Apache/mod_php and application-level PHP-FPM paths for the first vulnerability, and against a real-world Apache/mod_php application for the second. These were problems in PHP itself, not something an administrator could fix by simply updating a WordPress plugin. It was a fundamental and nasty security hole. How bad were the flaws? PHP’s advisories rate both vulnerabilities 9.2, or critical, under the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) v4.0. Exploitability depends on the PHP build, server configuration, extensions, and application behavior. The advisories do not establish that every PHP installation can be compromised. PHP released fixes in versions 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12. The potential exposure is substantial: As of November 11, W3Techs reported that PHP powered 68.8% of websites whose server-side programming language it could identify. According to the PHP Foundation’s account , a developer investigating issues from a 2024 security audit spotted the out-of-memory problem, but no concrete attack path was established then. Proposed fixes risked compatibility breaks, new denial-of-service problems, or changes across PHP extensions. On August 11, Calif researcher Ryan A. reported remote code execution from the same underlying problem. From that date, fixing it became the PHP Foundation security team’s top priority. OpenAI independently reported the same underlying flaw. Wiz supplied additional attack vectors on August 24, and OpenAI reported more on September 18. How the PHP security patch came apart In response, PHP’s maintainers coordinated fixes with researchers and distributors. Then details about the release process began leaking. On October 20, the CVE identifiers circulated publicly , accompanied by an incorrect release time and severity score. PHP responded by issuing a warning and…

articles.title: Google built an AI model that can’t write a sentence — and that’s the point
articles.content: Google’s new Gemini Decisions API, introduced Wednesday, is designed to handle the routine decisions that AI applications make thousands of times a day, with lower costs, and faster response times than traditional generative models. …the routine decisions that AI applications make thousands of times a day, with lower costs and faster response times than traditional generative models. Instead of using a generative model to work through each decision and produce a text response, the API uses a new model, Gemini Decision 1, to evaluate predefined options in a single pass. According to Google, response times range from 150 to 250 milliseconds for tested workloads, while pricing starts at $0.10 per million input tokens with no output-token charges. The release comes just weeks after OpenAI launched its own Decisions API , joining TypeSafe AI and Microsoft in a growing market for models built to make specific decisions without generating text. One pass, no generated text The API supports a 256,000-token context window and can evaluate up to 1,000 independent questions against a single input, including multimodal content. Its responses include probabilities and confidence scores that developers can use to select between predefined options, evaluate information against specific criteria and decide how an application should proceed. Google CEO Sundar Pichai described the model in a post on X as “built for closed-set choices,” while Google DeepMind product manager Min Choi and principal scientist Felix Yu characterized the API as providing “purpose-built primitives for bounded choices” in the launch announcement. Where Google already uses it Google is already using the model internally, including in Gemini Notebook, where real-time model and reasoning-level routing has reportedly reduced latency by up to 40%. Google Search also uses it to detect potentially adversarial behavior involving MCP tools. Benchmarks come from Google Google’s benchmark results show Gemini Decision 1 outperforming OpenAI’s GPT-6 Luna, although the competition with TypeSafe’s Jev 1.14 is closer. Logan Kilpatrick , who leads product for Google AI Studio and the Gemini API, described it on X as “our new frontier decision model in the Gemini API.” On JevBench, Google’s model scored 92.2%, compared with 90.9% for Luna and 90% for Jev. But Jev came out ahead on two of the seven shared tests and was cheaper to run, costing $0.68 for the full benchmark suite compared with $0.88 for Gemini Decision 1. Google’s model also recorded the lowest calibration error among those tested. All of the benchmark figures come from Google’s own testing, and independent evaluations have yet to establish how the models compare in production. SiliconANGLE also noted that Jev is cheaper than Google’s model on a per-token basis. All of the benchmark figures come from Google’s own testing, and independent evaluations have yet to establish how the models compare in production. What developers actually pay Developers only pay to send the shared context once, even when they’re asking multiple questions about it, although the questions themselves still count toward token usage. The API evaluates each question separately, so a workflow that needs to use one answer to decide what to ask next requires another call. Gemini Decision 1 is available through Google AI Studio , with a free prototyping tier and integrations through OpenRouter , LangChain, Vercel, and LiteLLM. Support for Gemini on Google Cloud is also planned, although Google has not announced a release date. Developers only pay to send the shared context once, even when they’re asking multiple questions about it… The post Google built an AI model that can’t write a sentence — and that’s the point appeared first on The New Stack .

articles.title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
articles.content: A critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module could allow unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute code and potentially take control of affected server processes. Tracked as CVE-2026-119618, the vulnerability affects Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 when HTTP/2 is enabled and is fixed in version 2.4.71. The Hacker News reports: The vendor's assessment, published yesterday, also says "public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit" against a server in its default configuration with mod_http2 enabled. It does not name or link that research. Security company Wiz said later that day that no exploit was available and that no exploitation in the wild had been reported. HTTP/2 runs only where the Protocols directive turns it on, as the module documentation explains. The directive uses h2 for HTTP/2 over TLS and h2c for HTTP/2 over plain TCP. It can be set for the whole server or for a single virtual host, so admins should check the server-wide setting and every virtual host. Standalone builds of the module, released on GitHub as mod_h2, are affected from version 2.0.8 through 2.0.42. Admins who run the Apache HTTP Server project's own releases should move to version 2.4.71, the fixed release named in its security advisory. That release also fixes a crash in mod_md, rated important, and a one-byte overwrite of stack memory in mod_vhost_alias, rated low. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: The AI boom was built around Jensen Huang. What happens now?
articles.content: Welcome to AI Decoded, Fast Company ‘s weekly newsletter that breaks down the most important news in the world of AI. I’m Mark Sullivan, a senior writer at Fast Company , covering emerging tech, AI, and tech policy. Sign up to receive this newsletter every week via email here . And if you have comments on this issue and/or ideas for future ones, drop me a line at sullivan@fastcompany.com , and follow me on X @thesullivan . Jensen Huang is out, and the repercussions are just beginning Who would have expected the AI Bubble to pop like this? Over an infidelity scandal. Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia CEO Thursday, built the company that supplied the chips that made the AI boom possible. He had the foresight to see the AI revolution coming, and formed the strategy to lock AI researchers and enterprises into his company’s CUDA software stack. Huang also used Nvidia’s growing chip sales windfall to prop up the growing AI industry in a dangerous way, bankrolling a webwork of AI startups, suppliers, infrastructure players, and other chip customers. Now, with a crisis of confidence in the chip company at the center, the whole AI buildout could come under considerable strain and potentially unravel. With all this at stake, one might wonder why Nvidia’s board and other stakeholders would want Huang to resign. But Jensen Huang’s affairs were more than marital transgressions. At least one of them had national security and geopolitical dimensions–Huang’s relationship with a Singapore-based tech executive who goes by the name Alice Huang. Not only was she a suspected Chinese spy but her company, Megaspeed, was suspected by the Commerce Department of helping funnel restricted Nvidia chips to China, the U.S.’s main rival in the AI race. A New York Times investigation last year found that Megaspeed’s offices in Singapore and Malaysia were largely empty, and Commerce Department officials who spoke to The Times said they found boxes of restricted Nvidia chips in a Megaspeed facility in Malaysia. It’s long been the policy of the U.S. government to reserve the fastest AI chips, most of them made by Nvidia, for U.S. and U.S.-friendly AI labs. Alice Huang had Chinese “honeypot” written all over her, but Jensen Huang never caught on, or chose not to. The second extramarital relationship to come to light is less harmful to Nvidia but establishes a pattern of infidelity that may go further than we currently know. It involved Kimberly Powell , an Nvidia VP who led Nvidia’s health industry business. That relationship, which had for months been discussed within Nvidia, was reported this week by the New York Times after reporters spoke to Nvidia employees. Nvidia’s code of conduct warns against employees “personal relationships” that might “create conflict.” It all seems so sudden. After months of hand wringing about the reality of the AI boom and the stability of the enormous amounts of investment money now being plowed into building out the infrastructure needed for AI, suddenly the man at the center of it all is gone, his 33 years of leading Nvidia over. And as Creative Strategies CEO Tim Bajarin told me, there’s nobody in the world with better field vision in the AI industry than Jensen Huang. “For much of the last decade he was the industry’s main spokesperson, explaining to customers, partners, governments and investors where computing was going and why,” says Bajarin, a long-time Silicon Valley analyst who knows Huang. “Few executives in technology have played that role . . . that is a real loss, for NVIDIA and for the ecosystem around it.” “Still, no one is irreplaceable, and the loss of a visionary is not the same as a change in strategy,” Bajarin says. “The vision Jensen laid out is already built into NVIDIA’s roadmap, its supply chain and its people, so we do not think his departure changes where the company is going.” Possible successors to Huang may have some pieces of the picture, but none have vision into the human…

articles.title: A 23M-Parameter Model Still Wins: 338 Embedding Models Ranked by Real Downloads
articles.content: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 , a 23M-parameter sentence-transformers model, was downloaded 177M times on Hugging Face in the last 30 days. That's 38% of all downloads across the 213 open-weight embedding models tracked by the TextModels directory , and more than the next four models combined. Below are all 338 embedding models in the directory: open weights ranked by downloads, then hosted APIs, Ollama builds and the historical models that started it all. Most "best embedding model" lists rank by benchmark score, like PremAI's ranking by MTEB score, cost and self-hosting . Benchmarks tell you what's best on paper. Downloads tell you what developers actually ship, and the two lists look very different. The sentence-transformers family's lead has a history. As HackerNoon's overview of embeddings for RAG puts it, "Simply said, the BERT model isn't the best for similarity search." SBERT fixed that by embedding each sentence separately so vectors can be computed once and compared fast, and its descendants still dominate the download charts. What the download data says Small and old beats big and new. The top two models by downloads, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (23M params) and BAAI's bge-small-en-v1.5 (33M), are tiny. For most production search, "fast and good enough" wins. The market is concentrated. The top 10 open-weight embedders account for 74% of the 470M monthly downloads in this list. Qwen is the newcomer to watch. Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B is already #9 with 9M monthly downloads, and its 4B and 8B siblings both clear 2.4M. Multilingual is mainstream. Five of the top 12 are multilingual: bge-m3, two paraphrase-multilingual models and two multilingual-e5 models. Vector databases ship their own builds. Qdrant's ONNX conversions and sparse models appear nine times, which shows how many teams get embeddings through their database instead of picking a model directly. How this list was built Everything comes from the TextModels directory's Embedding filter (338 models) as of November 11, 2026. Hugging Face entries are ranked by 30-day downloads pulled from the Hugging Face API. "Verified" means the TextModels directory fetched and confirmed that model's metrics per model. Hosted API models have no public download counts, so they're grouped by provider, alphabetically. Some hosted entries, like OpenAI's 001-series search models, are long retired. They stay in the list because people still search for them when migrating old pipelines. articles.title: GPT-4.5 Fooled 73% of Judges: 20 Turing Tests, Detectors and Fakes to Check Your AI Radar
articles.content: In a 2025 UC San Diego study, people picked GPT-4.5 as the human 73% of the time , more often than they picked the actual humans. ELIZA, a 1960s chatbot, scored 23%, slightly ahead of GPT-4o without a persona at 21%. Here are 20 tests from the Turing Test directory where you can check whether you still tell human from machine across chat, text, faces, art, voice and video. The Turing test used to be a thought experiment. Now it's a party game, a research method and a product category. Cameron Jones and Benjamin Bergen's three-party Turing test had 284 participants chat with a human and an AI at the same time and then pick the human. GPT-4.5 with a persona prompt won 73% of the time, and LLaMa-3.1-405B won 56%. The public versions tell the same story. AI21 Labs' "Human or Not?" game ran more than 10 million conversations, and players guessed right only 68% of the time . They were worse at spotting the bots (60%) than at spotting the humans (73%). And it isn't just chat: in a blind listening study covered on HackerNoon, listeners trying to pick out AI-composed piano music were "essentially guessing," at close to 50% accuracy. So test yourself. A note on what's included: not everything here is a quiz. Some are games, some are detectors that try to make the call for you, and some are the generators that make the fakes. To understand the Turing test in 2026, you need all three. Chat: can you tell who you're talking to? 1. Human or Not? by AI21 Labs. You get a two-minute chat with a stranger, then guess whether it was a person or a bot. It became the largest Turing test ever run, with more than 1.5 million participants . The research paper breaks down the tricks players used to unmask bots. 2. Loebner Prize . This was the original Turing test competition, held from 1991 according to its Wikipedia history . It's no longer running; its last winner was Mitsuku in 2019 . It belongs on any list because it shows how long "fooling the judges" was the goal, and how easy it looks now. 3. Bot or Not (Botometer) by Indiana University's OSoMe. It scores whether a social media account is a bot. It's a Turing test turned into a classifier. The live version shut down after X ended free researcher access, and the Botometer X archive only covers accounts created before June 2023. Text: human writer or language model? 4. GLTR (Giant Language model Test Room) from the MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab and Harvard NLP. Paste text and it colors each word by how predictable it was to a language model. It was built in 2019 to spot AI-written text , and it's still the best way to see why AI text "feels" smooth. 5. GPTZero . This is the AI-writing detector that teachers made famous. Run your own writing through it to see how often humans get flagged. HackerNoon's guide on how to detect text generated by AI explains what these tools measure. 6. Poem or AI? You read a poem and decide who wrote it. The research on this is humbling: in Porter and Machery's Scientific Reports study , 1,634 readers couldn't reliably tell ChatGPT poems from famous poets' , and they rated the AI poems higher. 7. NYT AI Article Quiz by The New York Times. Short passages, one question: human or AI? 8. WritersBrew AI Detector . A writing tool with a built-in check on whether a passage reads as machine-written. 9. Winograd Schema Challenge . This is the benchmark proposed as a better Turing test. Who does "it" refer to in "The trophy doesn't fit in the suitcase because it's too big"? It's easy for people. For years it was hard for machines. Faces: real photo or GAN? 10. Which Face Is Real? by Jevin West and Carl Bergstrom at the University of Washington. You see two faces and click the real one. It logged about 4 million plays in two weeks after its 2019 launch , and players were right about 70% of the time against StyleGAN fakes. 11. This Person Does Not Exist . This is the generator, not the quiz. Every refresh shows a face of someone who was never born. Look at the ears, teeth and backgrounds…

articles.title: Apple Adds Samsung Foldables to Trade-In Program
articles.content: Apple today revised its U.S. trade-in estimates, with increases for many older iPhones, reductions for several Pro models, and newly listed offers for six Samsung foldables. The iPhone 17 Pro has the largest dollar reduction among the affected iPhones, dropping $45 to a maximum of $740. The iPhone 17 Pro Max falls $30 to $855, while the iPhone Air and standard iPhone 17 each gain $30, bringing both to $615. Many older models recover some of the value lost in September's reductions . Most remain below their pre-September maximums, although the second-generation iPhone SE returns to $45, fully reversing its $5 cut. The following iPhone estimates have changed. articles.title: SkyW4lker Exposed: A Growing Microsoft 365 Phishing Threat to American Enterprises
articles.content: SkyW4lker (SkyW4lker x365 Sentinel) is an active device-code phishing kit targeting Microsoft 365 users in the United States, Europe, and other regions. By abusing Microsoft’s legitimate authentication process, the kit can give attackers access to corporate accounts without stealing passwords or bypassing MFA. This puts business emails, sensitive documents, and other Microsoft 365 resources at risk of unauthorized access. The ANY.RUN team identified 618 sandbox analyses related to SkyW4lker between June and October 21, 2026, with 46% of submissions coming from the United States . Activity increased from 20 analyses in June to 200 in September, highlighting the growing exposure of organizations relying on Microsoft 365. Key Takeaways SkyW4lker is distributed through phishing emails with a password-protected malicious attachment; the password is provided in the email body. After a chain of decoy pages, the victim reaches a page that asks for a Microsoft device code. The kit consists of a PHP backend and obfuscated JavaScript. Its main features are IP-based geolocation of visitors and periodic polling of the backend to check whether the victim has completed authentication. ANY.RUN’s powerful new capability, Related Threat Context , helped analysts accelerate the SkyW4lker investigation by instantly surfacing connections to previous sandbox analyses. This reduced manual correlation work, enabled faster expansion of the campaign cluster, and ultimately helped uncover the phishing kit’s administration panel. As a result, 618 analyses were identified over the past six months (as of October 21, 2026), with monthly submissions growing from 20 in June to 200 in September. They were submitted mainly by organizations in the technology, manufacturing, and government sectors, most often from the United States, India, Canada, and the United Kingdom. SkyW4lker shares its JavaScript modules, landing-URL format, and part of its hosting infrastructure with Gabagool, a credential phishing kit active since April 2026. We assess with high confidence that both kits were built by the same developer. SkyW4lker exploits routine business workflows, using contracts, invoices, and service proposals as phishing lures. By directing employees through familiar platforms and legitimate Microsoft authentication pages, attackers make malicious requests harder to distinguish from normal business activity. SkyW4lker Threat Overview Threat Type Phishing Kit Objective Microsoft 365 / OAuth credentials Capabilities JavaScript obfuscation (obfuscator.io), Device-Code phishing, Geolocation detection, IP-address detection, CAPTCHA verification Delivery Email attachments (.pdf, .docx, .xls/xlsx and others), redirection links and lure pages (including Google Maps, Google Images, Miro, Zoom and others) Motivation Possible financial Operator / brand SkyW4lker (SkyW4lker x365 Sentinel) Known links URL patterns: /session_public.php?action= /endpoints/confirm_visit.php /js/url_helper.js /js/endpoint.js /js/client_geo.js Activity window 2026-06 – now SkyW4lker Activity Across US Organizations The United States accounts for 47% of SkyW4lker-related sandbox submissions, more than twice the share of any other country. With the campaign exploiting legitimate Microsoft authentication processes and routine business communications, these findings raise concerns for US enterprises about how effectively existing security controls can identify suspicious activity before it leads to account compromise. What SkyW4lker Means for Enterprise Security SkyW4lker highlights several security risks that organizations need to account for when protecting business-critical systems and employee identities: Identity security gaps : Device-code phishing can succeed even when MFA is enabled, raising questions about whether existing authentication policies sufficiently restrict unnecessary access methods. Detection challenges: Attackers abuse legitimate Microsoft authentication flows and trusted…

articles.title: Microsoft has an image problem with November's Windows security update
articles.content: Printing with Windows has always been something of a choose-your-own-adventure, and November's security update has added another unwelcome plot twist: documents containing certain images might not print. The issue affects images rendered with a height or width of zero at the selected printing resolution. These might not be visible to users, but can form part of a document's watermarking or layout. After the update, those invisible objects can apparently make the printed document disappear too. Microsoft said: "The issue was observed when printing Microsoft Word documents using the Windows Graphics Device Interface (GDI), but printing from other applications might also be affected." According to the notification (WI1549472), most versions of Windows are affected, from the latest Windows 11 26H2 through Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2016. Windows Server from 2025 to 2016 is also affected. Users need not have added these objects themselves. Microsoft says document-generation tools can insert them even when no graphic is visible. Printer problems aren't the only issue requiring attention. After installation of the November 2026 security update, Microsoft warned that "certain Windows activation and licensing operations performed using the Software Licensing Management Tool (SLMGR) might fail." This one is a little more niche, but it could be a headache for affected administrators. It primarily affects organizations that use command-line tools or automated processes to manage Windows activation and licensing. "Affected devices might encounter error 0x80041008 , Invalid parameter ( SWbemObjectEx ), when running commands to activate Windows, configure Key Management Service (KMS), or manage product keys," Microsoft said. "The failure has been observed while executing the command ' slmgr.vbs /skms-domain ' and ' slmgr.vbs /ipk '." The notice (WI1549486) currently lists Windows 11 23H2, Windows 10 22H2 and 21H2, and Windows Server 2025, 2022, and 2019 as affected. The printing problem remains under investigation, but Microsoft says a fix for the activation issue is due in the coming days. Administrators needing an interim workaround must contact Microsoft Support for Business. ®

articles.title: AVA Foundation and Travala Unveil AVA 3.0: A Travala-First Roadmap
articles.content: Singapore, Singapore, November 12th, 2026/Chainwire/-- The AVA Foundation and Travala , the Binance-backed crypto travel booking platform, today announced AVA 3.0, accompanied by a roadmap that reinforces AVA token utility on Travala. As the AVA token’s primary commercial application, Travala is the focus of the new plan, which builds on AVA 2.0 and emphasises real-world travel products, transparent buybacks, and measurable member value. AVA 3.0 leads with existing products. The AVA Smart Program has more than 180,000 members, who lock AVA to save up to 13% on travel and receive other perks. Members can also pay for discounted travel with AVA and receive AVA rewards through the Travala AI Agent , which is live on BNB Chain in collaboration with Binance Pay. Backing the program is a monthly buyback. Each month, the AVA Foundation buys back AVA to replenish member giveback rewards, and Travala matches it and locks its share in the AVA Strategic Reserve. The AVA Buyback Multiplier scales Travala’s match between 1x and 3x as AVA givebacks grow, with a total monthly buyback potential of up to 4x AVA givebacks. More bookings generate more givebacks, and more givebacks mean bigger buybacks. To date, 5,604,414 AVA has been bought back by the Foundation, with 779,691.92 AVA (representing 1.1% of circulating supply) permanently locked in Travala’s AVA Strategic Reserve. 17.5% of AVA’s circulating supply is locked as the ecosystem targets a long-term goal of 30%. Two launches are next. Increased AVA lock levels for new Smart members are expected in November, while existing members keep their current locks and can use the new Smart Boost feature to increase their AVA locks and potential rewards. AVA+ Partners follows, with the launch expected in Q1 2027. It will allow partner projects to lock AVA for their tokens to be accepted as payment on Travala. The Foundation is exploring several further ideas for 2027 and beyond, including AI booking agents that recognise Smart membership tiers to apply membership benefits, curated travel specials available exclusively in AVA, and VIP travel concierge access based on AVA holdings. “Through every market since we started, one thing has held true: AVA is at its best when it's used,” said Juan Otero, Travala CEO and co-founder, and Steven Hipwell, Travala co-founder and AVA Foundation Lead Contributor. “AVA 3.0 isn’t about grand promises; it’s about evolving what already works.” The AVA token and all existing memberships, locks, and rewards continue as normal. Partnerships beyond Travala will be assessed where they deliver clear commercial value. Read the full AVA 3.0 Roadmap that details all upcoming launches and areas of exploration. Disclaimer This release contains information about current plans and areas of exploration. Each new product is announced as live only after it has been built and approved. Its mention is not a commitment to launch. Travala and the AVA Foundation are separate organisations with distinct responsibilities. This release is for information only and is not financial advice, or an offer, solicitation, or inducement to acquire, hold, or lock AVA. It is not directed at persons in the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates, or any jurisdiction where distribution would be unlawful. References to Travala are to TravelFront and its group companies. See the full AVA utility token disclaimer and the AVA MiCA white paper . About the AVA Foundation The AVA Foundation oversees the AVA token ecosystem, including the AVA Smart Program, AVA token, and Travel Tiger NFTs. The AVA token functions as the key to accessing the AVA Smart Program, which provides travel perks and other benefits to Travala customers, such as AVA payment discounts and AVA loyalty rewards. AVA tokenises the concept of loyalty reward programs using blockchain technology, bringing web3 to traditional loyalty models. For more information, visit: www.avafoundation.org . articles.title: President Trump says Apple’s Tim Cook is the only man to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
articles.content: President Donald Trump has said that retired Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia, just hours after it was announced that the latter had resigned in the wake of a series of scandals. Taking to his Truth Social platform, the President said , "NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend! President DONALD J. TRUMP." Nvidia's board of directors announced on Wednesday that Huang had resigned following the revelation that he conducted an extramarital affair with a Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset , and a further affair with Nvidia Vice President of Health Care, Kimberly Powell. Colette Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, will serve as Interim CEO while the company looks for a replacement. Naturally, names have been floated as potential successor candidates, including Apple's Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji. With Nvidia at the center of the global explosion in AI, Huang and Trump have enjoyed a close relationship that routinely makes news headlines. Trump previously described Huang as 'utterly visionary' in regard to his views on tariffs and rescinding President Biden's AI Diffusion Rule . President Trump's name has been mentioned in the ongoing Huang affair scandal. Notably, it is alleged that while U.S. intelligence believed that Huang had been the target of a Chinese honeypot operation , reports claim that President Trump was briefed on the matter but chose not to do anything with the information, so as not to affect Nvidia's sales or antagonize China. Congress has summoned Jensen Huang to appear before the Select Committee on the CCP , with lawmakers threatening to issue Huang with a subpoena if he doesn't agree to attend a closed-door meeting voluntarily. Tim Cook is currently the Executive Chair of Apple's board, having served as the company's CEO from 2011 to 2026. During his tenure, he oversaw the launch of a plethora of Apple services, including Apple Music and Apple TV, while expanding into new product categories such as Apple Watch and AirPods. Nvidia's share price plunged more than 10 percentage points at the open on Wednesday, but recovered much of that ground as traders looked to take advantage of the dip in Nvidia's share price. The company will report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results next week, on Tuesday, November 17.
articles.author: Stephen Warwick

articles.title: Migrate to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with your coding agent
articles.content: With a customer-managed knowledge base on Amazon Bedrock , you provision and scale the vector store, tune the embedding model and index settings, and plan capacity for each new data source. The migration guide in the Agent Toolkit for AWS helps you migrate to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base . Managed Knowledge Base takes over that work and adds new retrieval capabilities, and your team keeps control of the content and the application that uses it. Moving a production knowledge base means your team maps its configuration, creates the replacement, ingests content, updates the application’s retrieval call, and validates retrieval before switching traffic. To help, we added a knowledge base migration guide to the amazon-bedrock skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS . The guide gives your coding agent the context to plan the migration with you, starting with read-only discovery and a plan you review line by line. On your approval, the agent creates the new knowledge base and its data sources alongside the original, or writes a migrated infrastructure as code (IaC) template for your pipeline. Ingestion and updating your application’s Retrieve calls stay with you, and your agent can walk you through both. In this post, we explain why we recommend the move and how the migration guide works, review the prerequisites, install the skill, plan a migration, update the application’s retrieval call, and validate retrieval before cutover. Why move to Managed Knowledge Base We recommend Managed Knowledge Base because it balances ease of use, retrieval accuracy, and cost. AWS runs the store With a Managed Knowledge Base, Amazon Bedrock handles ingestion, storage, indexing, and retrieval, and the store scales automatically as your content grows. Hybrid search, which combines keyword and semantic matching, is always on, with no index to configure. The knowledge base includes a managed embedding model, a managed reranker, and a built-in parser for multimodal file types. You can still bring your own Amazon Bedrock embedding model when you create the knowledge base. On each retrieval request, you choose the managed reranker, an Amazon Bedrock reranking model, or no reranking. The managed reranker requires the managed embedding model. Built-in capabilities Managed Knowledge Base includes capabilities you’d otherwise build yourself: Native connectors ingest content directly from sources such as Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), Microsoft SharePoint, and Atlassian Confluence. For the current list, see supported connectors . After the first full sync, later syncs pick up only changes, on demand or on a schedule. The Managed Knowledge Base includes a deletion safeguard to help protect against accidental bulk removal of indexed content. Access control list (ACL) awareness ingests document permissions with the content, so retrieval returns only what the signed-in user can access. For connectors that support it, such as Microsoft SharePoint and Atlassian Confluence, a real-time check against the source also catches permission changes since the last sync. ACL awareness doesn’t authenticate users, so your application must verify and pass the user’s identity. Agentic retrieval answers questions that a single search can’t by handling multi-part questions and retrieving iteratively. It can search more than one knowledge base in a single request. Integration with AgentCore Gateway , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, exposes your knowledge base as a target. Any client that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) can then query the knowledge base, and the gateway handles authentication. Resource-based policies let applications in other AWS accounts use one team’s knowledge base. Scope each policy to the specific roles that call the knowledge base, and grant only the actions they use, such as bedrock:Retrieve . Agentic retrieval, AgentCore Gateway integration, and resource-based policies are not available on customer-managed knowledge bases.…
articles.author: Josh DeMuth

articles.title: ‘We’re still here’: Technology Access Foundation keeps opening doors for students of color, 30 years later
articles.content: TAF co-founders Trish Millines Dziko, left, and Jill Hull Dziko receive flowers from Sherry Williams, TAF’s executive director of operations, at the organization’s 30th anniversary celebration in Seattle in October. (GeekWire Photo / Todd Bishop) Editor’s note: Microsoft, which underwrites GeekWire’s Impact Series, is a longtime TAF supporter. The company was not involved in this story. Back in the fall of 2002, then-Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer wrapped up a luncheon speech at Seattle’s Rainier Club by asking a question that few people in the room expected — least of all the college freshman he directed it to. “So you want an internship this summer?” he asked Miya McClain , as she remembers it. She was Miya Sneed then, 18 and homesick at Mills College in Oakland, Calif. She had come home to speak for Technology Access Foundation , the Seattle nonprofit where she had gone from knowing nothing about computers to building software and leading a team of student interns. Earlier in the luncheon program, she had shown the crowd a scheduling system she built for TAF. Microsoft had planned the offer in advance and already had her resume, but she had no idea what was coming. A Seattle Times photographer caught the look of shock on her face, and the photo ran the next day on the front of the newspaper’s business section. That internship, the first of two, led to a full-time job at Microsoft after college. She spent eight years there before moving into product leadership roles at Nordstrom, Cisco and Smartsheet. Today McClain is senior vice president of product management at SumerSports, a sports analytics company. “Most of my jobs came through connections with TAF,” she said, crediting the organization for repeatedly “opening doors I didn’t even know could be opened.” Then-Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer gives Miya McClain (then Miya Sneed) a thumbs-up after offering her an internship at a TAF luncheon in October 2002, left. At right, McClain today. (TAF Photo, left; LinkedIn Photo, right) That’s the path Trish Millines Dziko had in mind when she left Microsoft 30 years ago to start TAF with her partner, Jill Hull Dziko: teach kids of color to work with technology, and get them hired by tech companies. But about eight years in, she saw a problem. TAF’s interns were thriving, she said, but many couldn’t get into college computer science or engineering courses because their high schools had already steered them into lower-level math and science. To change that, TAF would need to reach students by sixth grade, inside the schools. So TAF went into public education. The organization, which marked its 30th anniversary Oct. 1, now co-manages a public middle and high school in Federal Way, Wash., and coaches teachers in other public schools. “No matter what our kids do, we teach them to use STEM skills. They have to critically think. They have to solve problems. … They have to communicate. They have to lead.” Trish Millines Dziko Executive director, Technology Access Foundation Working with entire schools, rather than kids who signed up for a tech program, changed the goal, too. The focus now is on skills students can use in any field, whether or not it’s tech. Students learn science, technology, engineering and math through projects that combine subjects and put classroom lessons to use. In 2020, for example, two students at TAF’s Federal Way school turned a gardening robot into a model 3D printer using a cake-frosting syringe, a threaded rod and a motor, as GeekWire reported at the time . “What we want to make sure is, no matter what our kids do, we teach them to use STEM skills,” Millines Dziko said. “They have to critically think. They have to solve problems. … They have to communicate. They have to lead.” The shift has cost TAF money. The organization has missed out on larger funding opportunities, Millines Dziko…

articles.title: Elizabeth Banks and Ted Danson team up for Apple TV's 'She's Fine'
articles.content: A brand new comedy series starring Elizabeth Banks is set to land on Apple TV on January 27, showing just how crazy life can get after divorce. Image credit: Apple "She's Fine" follows Heidi (Banks), a recent divorcee, as she starts over for herself and her kids. Things go awry when she finds herself coordinating her father's retirement community sexcapades and forges an uneasy alliance with his girlfriend's single son. The ensemble cast also features Rob Delaney, Ted Danson, Katey Sagal, Jared Goldstein, Spencer Moss, Titus Collier and Thaddaeus Collier. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

articles.title: Beyond 12 Columns: Designing Layouts With Personality
articles.content: Too many websites look alike. They use familiar layouts, repeat the same patterns, and often leave little impression once you’ve moved on. Andy Clarke explores how understanding a company’s story can lead to more distinctive designs, using modular and compound grids to create layouts with character. Beyond 12 Columns: Designing Layouts With Personality originally handwritten and published with love on CSS-Tricks . You should really get the newsletter as well.

articles.title: Seattle’s Allen Institute helps create a ‘Rosetta Stone’ for brain cells to unlock clues to disease
articles.content: The structures of the basal ganglia illuminated as part of the Human Mammalian Brain Atlas, a three-dimensional reference atlas to facilitate brain research and collaboration among organizations and scientists. (Allen Institute Photo / Ashwin Bhandiwad) A coalition of 56 institutions across nine countries is publishing groundbreaking research today on the basal ganglia — a group of brain structures that help control movement, emotions, motivation and habits. The region is linked to psychiatric and degenerative disorders, including schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and Parkinson’s disease. Michael Hawrylycz, principal investigator with the Seattle-based Allen Institute. (Allen Institute Photo) The scientist have produced a biological Rosetta Stone that creates a shared system for naming and describing cells in the basal ganglia across species. The goal is to help researchers compare findings, collaborate and accelerate their understanding of this essential brain region. “This is groundwork that is necessary to really make progress,” said Michael Hawrylycz , principal investigator with the Seattle-based Allen Institute who helped organize the consortium. The project, called the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network, or BICAN, produced a basal ganglia atlas that is publicly available for basic researchers, clinicians and others to use. The research is being presented in a package of 26 articles in a special issue of the journal Cell . The data comes from humans, macaques, marmoset and mice. One of the benefits of comparing the basal ganglia between species is understanding which components are uniquely human, providing potential insights into neurological diseases. Despite the critical and wide-ranging roles, the basal ganglia is relatively small — it’s about 2% of the brain with a volume roughly the size of a large gumball. For the project, the researchers pulled information from 25.5 million brain cells, including 21 million human cells. They used a variety of techniques to tease out insights, including RNA sequencing to identify gene activity from single cells in precise locations; epigenomic studies revealing where genes are switched on or off; and measurements of electrical activity combined with cell shape and genetic information. It’s a lot of data to stitch together and make sense of, Hawrylycz said. “AI is a perfect tool” for the job, he said, because it excels at finding patterns. Highlights from the studies include: The identification of a new type of brain cell linked to schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. The development of a more targeted gene therapy that showed promise in reducing Parkinson’s-related tremors in animal models. The characterization of genetic changes in a specific basal ganglia cell types that potentially play a role in autism. The discovery of age-related patterns in gene expression across multiple cell types that researchers could use to predict an individual’s age. The findings could help guide future treatments, but the work remains basic research rather than clinical research, Hawrylycz said. The new research is the first major installment of the third phase of a brain-mapping effort that began in 2014. The first phase demonstrated that scientists could analyze individual cells on a large scale. The second produced an atlas of the mouse brain. BICAN aims to create a standardized atlas describing cells throughout the brains of humans and other primates. Hawrylycz said the work is expected to take another two or three years.

articles.title: Mac malware doesn't need a security flaw when users do the work
articles.content: Bitdefender's latest Mac threat report shows adware gaining ground as attackers increasingly use browser scams to trick users into bypassing Apple's security protections. MacBook Air M5 Bitdefender's September 2026 macOS Threat Landscape Report analyzes more than 1.5 billion security events collected between August 2025 and July 2026. Excluding web and document threats, adware rose from 22.6% of detections in the previous report to 34.4%. Trojans remained the largest category at 45.2%, down from 51.8%. Potentially unwanted apps also fell from 25.3% to 20.4%. The shift reflects the growing prominence of malicious ads , browser redirects, and deceptive software installers that trick users into compromising their Macs. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

articles.title: Elon Musk says it ‘would be an honor’ to hire ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
articles.content: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO two weeks after his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy was revealed by intelligence sources and a day after his affair with an Nvidia vice president became publicly known. But hours before this move, when it was just rumored that the Nvidia board was planning to oust him , Elon Musk had already stated his willingness to hire the former Nvidia chief on X . A random X user posted, “Elon please hire Jensen,” to which the billionaire replied, “That would be an honor.” @zerohedge That would be an honor November 12, 2026 Despite the scandals that Jensen is currently facing, he still has the engineering know-how, deep knowledge of the industry and its inner workings, plus multiple connections across the world, which would be extremely valuable for any company looking to break into the semiconductor industry. This is exactly what Elon Musk is doing with his Terafab project, which he first mentioned in November 2025 . Jensen Huang even warned that this was going to be a challenge, pointing out that “the engineering, the science, and the artistry of doing what TSMC does for a living is extremely hard.” Nevertheless, Musk poured his resources into the project, with construction on the Terafab facility in full swing and with plans to hit volume chip production by the second half of 2028 . Musk himself said that the site targets a production capacity of a million wafers a month by 2032. Tesla has an ambitious AI accelerator roadmap , and SpaceX has even touted making its own GPUs in the future . We still don’t know what Jensen Huang’s plans are, but even though he’s no longer a part of the Nvidia board and its leadership, Jensen and his wife, Lori, still jointly own approximately 800 million Nvidia shares through various trusts and LLCs, while Huang himself personally owns around 70 million Nvidia shares. Aside from that, he still has an outstanding invitation from Congress to discuss Nvidia’s security protocols, which could turn into a subpoena if he snubs them, although we don’t know how his resignation would affect the closed-door meeting. There’s also a reported FBI investigation into his relationship with Alice Huang , the Megaspeed executive who was allegedly instrumental in the import of $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia AI GPUs into China and is suspected of working with China’s Ministry of State Security . Jensen Huang is just the latest in the long list of executives who resigned or were ousted from their leadership position because of a relationship or an affair with a subordinate. This includes former Boeing CEO Harry Stonecipher in 2005, HP CEO Mark Hurd in 2010, Intel CEO Brian Krzanich in 2018, and former McDonald’s CEO Steve Easterbrook in 2019. Musk himself is known to have had relationships with subordinates from his various companies, and that he has even fathered four children with Shivon Zilis, a top executive at Neuralink who started working at Tesla in 2017, through IVF. It’s still not confirmed if Musk’s reply is a serious offer for Jensen Huang. But if the former Nvidia chief ever decides to work for Musk on his Terafab project, then Jensen could put his effort and expertise into turning it into a formidable competitor to Nvidia.

articles.title: An expert in espionage on spies, honeypots, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
articles.content: Nvidia announced early Thursday morning that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned from the company. The updates come after reports that Huang had been having affairs with an alleged Chinese spy, as well as an executive who reported to him at the company. The scandal has spurred myriad national security concerns and sent Nvidia stock tumbling. For the chipmaker—which sources some 80% of the world’s GPUs—Huang’s exit marks the loss of an executive who led the company through an AI craze and to record profits. But for the United States, and the tech industry more broadly, the scandal raises concerns about ongoing attempts by spies to steal valuable intellectual property and compromise the country’s leading technology executives. “I can vouch for the lack of concern by senior executives about such matters,” Matt Brazil, an expert in espionage now writing about the topic and a former U.S. Army officer, corporate security investigator, and expert control official, told Fast Company. “They will freely spend money to increase revenue but are far less enthusiastic about outlays to protect revenues, reduce losses, or promote security awareness.” Brazil, who is also a senior fellow at the Jamestown Foundation, a global analysis firm, emailed with Fast Company from Melbourne, Australia about the prevalence of honeypot schemes, the threat of espionage to tech companies, and what steps boards take to investigate their top executives. This email interview has been edited for length. How common are these kinds of honeypot schemes, particularly those backed by the Chinese government and targeting American tech executives? Unfortunately, they may be very common. For example, there are parallels in this case with the problem from a decade ago involving the Chinese agent—or officer— Christine Fang . Ms. Fang targeted California and other politicians and used sexual exploitation to gather information and build influence. However, this case regarding [Alice Huang, the leader of Singapore-based Megaspeed and alleged spy for the Chinese government] was potentially far more successful because of who Jensen Huang is, what he knows, his access to technology, and his connections, including in Silicon Valley and with the White House. What do you imagine the target was: Nvidia intellectual property, classified intel from the Trump administration, or a voice in Washington in favor of loosening chip restrictions? Something else? The target could be all of the above. If Ms. Huang had access to Jensen’s devices during an overnight stay, all of the above could have been compromised because there is no telling what was on his phone and laptop hard drive. A national-level security agency could have given her devices to quickly copy a hard drive in the time it takes for Jensen to be in the shower. As someone who regularly texted the president, his devices could have practically anything because of Mr. Trump’s habit of sharing sensitive information with those he trusts. What kind of training and oversight do tech executives have to prevent this kind of stuff? Very little unless there is leadership from the top to spend the money and time needed to train executives. From nearly two decades in international business, I can vouch for the lack of concern by senior executives about such matters. They will freely spend money to increase revenue but are far less enthusiastic about outlays to protect revenues, reduce losses, or promote security awareness. They are very conservative about thorough background investigations, for example, except for a few “positions of trust” that generally are connected to revenue (i.e. the CFO). The people who handle technology and operations tend to be trusted until they violate the company’s code of conduct. Are you warned about honeypots and other similar espionage schemes when you get security clearance? Is this something company boards require—or should require? Yes, people in government are trained about this…

articles.title: Build composable, interoperable multi-agent systems with A2A on AWS
articles.content: Agents in multi-agent systems that span organizational boundaries often need to collaborate in a composable, interoperable way, with agents that other organizations build and run. They need a way to discover each other, communicate, and exchange tasks without exposing internals or requiring the same framework on both sides. The Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol addresses this constraint. Without A2A, building composable multi-agent systems across organizational boundaries requires custom integration code for each customer and framework. Independent software vendors (ISVs) can instead build composable, interoperable agents that work with the A2A-compatible frameworks their customers already use. While we frame this post around the ISV use case, the pattern also applies to organizations that expose agents across boundaries, whether to partners, customers, or internal teams that use different frameworks. As your system grows, you add skills by registering Agent Cards with the orchestrator, without changing the agents already running. In this post, we walk through a deployed reference architecture on AWS. A LangChain-based enterprise orchestrator communicates with a Strands Agents-based software as a service (SaaS) agent across organizational boundaries using A2A, with the enterprise and the SaaS provider in separate AWS accounts. Neither side depends on the other’s framework or SDK, and the two sides share no secrets. We cover the architecture and implementation patterns, then deploy the system from three Jupyter notebooks and run an end-to-end test. The A2A protocol is now a Linux Foundation project , and AWS is among the organizations that support it. With A2A, agents can discover each other, negotiate tasks, and collaborate across organizational boundaries through a standardized protocol. The protocol uses existing authentication standards such as OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) for cross-boundary security, and is designed to work across A2A-compatible frameworks. In Open Protocols for Agent Interoperability Part 4: Inter-Agent Communication on A2A , we introduced A2A concepts and demonstrated two Strands agents communicating using the protocol on AWS. That post established the foundation with Agent Card discovery, structured task execution, and the A2A server pattern. This post builds on that foundation with cross-framework interoperability, cross-organizational trust boundaries, and OAuth in both directions. Solution overview Three agents run in two AWS accounts, one for the enterprise and one for the SaaS provider. The A2A protocol connects them, with OAuth authentication in both directions. Each account has its own Amazon Cognito user pool, so each side authenticates with its own identity provider. Figure 1: A2A agents across an enterprise account and a SaaS provider account During onboarding, the enterprise and the SaaS provider exchange only public values, such as identity provider URLs, client IDs, scopes, and endpoint URLs. Each side then trusts tokens from the other side’s user pool, and no secrets are shared. After onboarding, each request follows these steps: The enterprise app gets an access token from the enterprise’s Amazon Cognito user pool. The app sends a question over HTTPS to the user API in Amazon API Gateway, then polls for the answer. Amazon API Gateway forwards the request privately, through a VPC link and an internal Network Load Balancer, to the Enterprise Orchestrator, a LangChain agent. When its model decides that the question needs a compliance scan, the orchestrator gets its own token from the enterprise user pool, using a client secret stored in AWS Secrets Manager . The orchestrator sends an A2A request to the compliance SaaS agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, using the skill it read from the agent’s Agent Card at startup. The compliance agent checks the enterprise context agent’s Agent Card at the callback URL registered at onboarding, then gets a token from the SaaS provider’s own…

articles.title: I Used AI Coding Tools for 30 Days. Here’s What Made Me Faster (And What Didn’t)
articles.content: A few weeks ago, I caught myself spending 40 minutes writing a form validation schema I had written a dozen times before. I wasn’t learning anything. I was just typing. That was the moment I decided to run an experiment: for 30 days, I would use AI coding assistants on every project I touched, and I would log what saved me time and what quietly wasted it. I expected a magic productivity boost. What I got was more nuanced. Some habits made me noticeably faster. Others made me slower while feeling productive, which is the worst combination. This is the honest breakdown, including the mistakes. The Setup I mostly build web apps with React and Node.js, with the occasional Python script for automation. During the experiment, I worked on three things: A client dashboard (React + Express) An internal automation script (Python) An older codebase I joined mid-month and had to understand quickly I used ChatGPT, Claude, and GitHub Copilot alongside VS Code. To keep myself honest, I kept a plain notes file with three columns: the task, my estimate without help, and the actual time taken. It isn’t scientific, but it was enough to spot patterns. What Worked 1. Handing off the boring parts first The biggest win was boilerplate: config files, validation, CRUD endpoints, regex, date formatting. I know exactly what I want in these tasks, but typing them out is tedious. Here is a real example. I needed to validate a signup request. Writing it by hand meant checking the docs for the right syntax, handling each field and then writing error messages. About 15 minutes. My prompt: “Express 4, Node 20. Write a validation middleware for a signup route using Joi. Fields: name (2-50 chars), email, password (min 8, at least one number). Return 400 with a clear message for each failure.” I got a working first draft in under a minute, reviewed it, tweaked two messages and moved on. Total: about 3 minutes. const Joi = require('joi'); const signupSchema = Joi.object({ name: Joi.string().min(2).max(50).required(), email: Joi.string().email().required(), password: Joi.string().min(8).pattern(/\d/).required() }); function validateSignup(req, res, next) { const { error } = signupSchema.validate(req.body, { abortEarly: false }); if (error) { return res.status(400).json({ errors: error.details.map(d => d.message) }); } next(); } The rule I settled on: if I can explain the task in two sentences and I’d be bored writing it, hand it off. 2. Writing prompts like bug reports My early prompts were lazy: “fix this error.” The answers were generic and often wrong. Then I started including four things every time: The language, framework and version What I expected to happen What actually happened, with the exact error message Only the relevant code, not the whole file Compare these two prompts: “My API is not working.” “I’m using Express 4 with Node 20. This POST route returns a 500 when the body is empty. Here’s the handler and the error log. I expect a 400 with a validation message.” The second one gets a useful answer on the first try almost every time. Good prompting turned out to be the same skill as writing a good bug report, and that skill makes you a better teammate even without any tools. 3. Understanding code I didn’t write This surprised me the most. When I joined the older codebase, I pasted unfamiliar functions and asked, “Explain what this does, what its inputs are and what could break it.” I still read the code myself afterwards, but having a first explanation to check against cut my onboarding time from what I estimated would be a week to about three days. It also helped me find a function that silently swallowed errors, which nobody on the team knew about. 4. Finding edge cases I would have missed I’m not great at imagining how my own code will fail. Asking for “10 edge cases for this function that might break it” gave me inputs I wouldn’t have tried: empty arrays, null values, unicode characters, extremely large numbers, duplicate entries. Three of those…

articles.title: United Airlines wants you to check in, not your chatbot
articles.content: United Airlines has become the latest company to slap restrictions on unauthorized third-party AI agents, warning that the bots could make unintended purchases, expose customer data, or bypass checks requiring human acknowledgment. The airline announced restrictions covering both its own digital platforms and indirect access through travel agencies and aggregators, with changes to its booking, ticketing, and distribution policies. United says automated actions could violate aviation regulations, citing the requirement for a human acknowledgment during check-in that bags contain no banned substances. A bot cheerfully ticking the box isn't quite the passenger confirmation it has in mind. And then there is the worry that "sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles." United would also rather customers use its own app than turn third-party assistants loose on its systems. AI agents are pitched as a way to outsource life's minutiae, and it's difficult to navigate the web without tripping over a breathless influencer explaining why you need one, or dozens, or hundreds of virtual personal assistants. The thing is that operating these assistants requires care and thought. Earlier this year, British mathematician Professor Hannah Fry conducted a cautionary experiment in which she gave an AI agent a bank card, and a bit too much agency, to see what it would do. Passwords were coughed up, and some ill-considered purchases were made. Still, as Fry said of the agent, dubbed Cassandra, "don't let her incompetence fool you, because these things are getting better fast." Last month, reports emerged of major US banks blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside accounts and taking actions on behalf of the customer. This month, several UK banks were reported to have followed suit. United stated: "Corporate leaders in the banking and retail industries have taken similar actions regarding AI agents and we encourage others to consider measures that preserve the data and security of their customers and strengthen safety." The Register asked United Airlines how it planned to implement the blocking. There are a few options, including physical biometric confirmation for actions or checking for signs of automated browser driving. Amazon has also moved against unauthorized AI agents, blocking Meta's Muse (the "AI that gets it done," according to Meta's marketing) in September . The airline has yet to respond. ®

articles.title: 17 Agent Skills Analyze Single-Cell RNA-seq So You Don't Have to Script It
articles.content: GPTomics' bioSkills includes 17 MIT-licensed single-cell skills that cover the whole analysis: preprocessing, doublet detection, clustering, annotation, batch integration, trajectories and cell-cell communication. They work across Scanpy, Seurat and SingleCellExperiment, and they tell the agent which method fits the data, such as Harmony versus scVI or CellTypist versus SingleR. All 17 install with one command from Cuttlefish.MD , HackerNoon's license-checked skills marketplace. They follow the open Agent Skills standard , so they run in Claude Code, Codex CLI and 30+ other tools , and each is indexed in HackerNoon's SKILL.md Library . articles.title: AI-related job creation to outpace losses by 2030, says Gartner
articles.content: Wider use of AI within organizations will lead to more jobs being created than are lost by 2030, according to Gartner. Around 10.6 million jobs will be added globally (excluding China and India) by the end of the decade, with 8.9 million lost, according to a Gartner report — a net increase of 1.7 million jobs. At most, around 1.8% of the workforce will experience job losses attributable to AI during this time period, Gartner predicts. At the same time, a total of 5 million jobs will cumulatively be deferred during this period. This refers to jobs that “would otherwise have been created, but where AI is used as an excuse to restrain hiring,” according to Gartner’s report . Gartner considers deferred jobs as separate from jobs lost. “Job deferrals were the first effect felt from AI,” said John Lovelock, Gartner distinguished VP analyst and chief forecaster, with “companies holding off hiring open positions until the effects of AI projects were known.” A recent KPMG survey of 400 US CEOs showed that 89% expect to increase headcount over the next three years, which KPMG US CEO Tim Walsh linked to AI adoption in an Axios interview last month. For now, though, job losses attributed to AI outpace those created, according to Gartner’s study. During 2026, there were 2.2 million jobs lost due to AI, and 1.6 million gained. Lovelock expects the situation will change in the coming years, however, as organizations see greater success with AI deployments. “This will reverse once AI is through the Trough of Disillusionment ,” he said, in reference to Gartner’s Hype Cycle framework . Gartner The number of jobs deferred is also forecast to fall in the coming years. During 2026, 1.3 million people experienced a delay in hiring, down from 2.1m last year, according to Gartner’s forecast, with 400,000 jobs forecast to be deferred during 2030. The impact of AI will vary across sectors, with the technology industry expected to see the largest net job gains compared to other areas, such as public sector and asset-intensive industries. Gartner predicts the creation of 1.9 million new technology jobs by 2030, with 400,000 lost. Services sector jobs — such as in financial services — are forecast to see a similar level of job creation, alongside large numbers of losses. A similar Gartner report in 2025 predicted that more services jobs would be lost than created, but the analyst firm now forecasts a net increase as demand grows for data- and system-oriented skills. “This industry is most able to improve productivity of employees and increase employment,” said Lovelock. The Gartner report doesn’t specifiy which job roles will benefit from greater adoption of AI, though the analyst firm expects some portion of newly created jobs will be “directly linked to the implementation, maintenance and scaling of AI.” Government jobs are expected to see the largest net job loss of any industry, said Lovelock. “Without the incentive of revenue growth or industry transformation, governments are expected to focus on the AI benefits of efficiencies and staff reduction,” he said. Entry-level positions are expected to be the hardest hit by job deferrals, said Lovelock. “We do see many of the deferred positions being hired after a 12- to 24-month delay,” he said. “Unfortunately, some deferred positions do transition into job loss. In most industries and positions, the employee experience pyramid will skew toward senior positions.” In a separate report from September, Gartner forecast that 30% of positions eliminated by AI-related layoffs will be refilled by 2029, on average. For enterprise-sized organizations, the figure is likely to be higher, at around 40%.

articles.title: The death of the 14-day patch: Surviving machine-speed vulnerability discovery
articles.content: For decades, enterprise vulnerability management ran on human time: A security researcher manually dissected a binary, traced execution paths, built a proof of concept, and filed a coordinated disclosure. Engineering leads evaluated the CVSS score and prioritized the fi before working it into an upcoming sprint schedule. Then, finally, they shipped the update. That deliberate cadence is a thing of the past. In the first nine months of 2026, publishers recorded 75,242 CVEs , representing roughly 20% of all vulnerabilities published since the CVE program was established in 1999 . The acceleration is steepening: according to the Cyber Strategy Institute, nearly 38,000 of those flaws surfaced in Q3 alone. “The pace of vulnerability discovery has outpaced the human capacity to remediate it. Engineering organizations face a stark operational reality: the traditional two-week patch cycle is dead.” The pace of vulnerability discovery has outpaced the human capacity to remediate it. Engineering organizations face a stark operational reality: the traditional two-week patch cycle is dead. Why vulnerabilities exploded in 2026 This surge is not caused by developers writing worse code. It is the direct result of vulnerability hunting transforming from an artisan craft into an autonomous, distributed compute problem. Autonomous codebase traversal: Legacy SAST tools flooded dashboards with noisy pattern matches. Modern agentic security systems run full-context semantic analysis: cloning repositories, tracing asynchronous data flows across microservices, constructing dynamic exploit payloads in sandboxes, and confirming exploitability before ever raising an alert. Exhaustive compute at scale: Compute does not tire. Swarms of automated agents continuously traverse open-source package registries and public repositories, decompiling transitive dependencies, auditing legacy C/C++ utilities, and testing modern Go, Rust, and Node.js runtimes for concurrency bugs, deserialization flaws, and memory leaks. Focus on foundational infrastructure: Autonomous discovery focuses heavily on high-leverage software targets, identity layers, reverse proxies, parsers, and container runtimes. “This surge is not caused by developers writing worse code. It is the direct result of vulnerability hunting transforming from an artisan craft into an autonomous, distributed compute problem.” When machines search exhaustively across the entire public software graph, they will discover every reachable flaw. The operational cascade The deluge of machine-discovered CVEs creates severe structural friction across risk management, engineering velocity, and compliance: The exposure gap becomes unmanageable: As detailed in analysis on the expanding CVE exposure gap , the critical hazard is the elapsed time between public exploit discovery and downstream production deployment. When agentic frameworks generate working zero-day or N-day exploits within hours of a code push, a multi-day patching window is an open door. Alert paralysis and triage debt: Engineering teams are trapped between CVSS scores (which measure theoretical severity) and EPSS metrics (which predict real-world exploitation likelihood). Discerning whether an alert represents an unreachable helper function or an active, weaponizable zero-click flaw has turned routine triage into continuous crisis management. Compliance and audit deadlock: Frameworks like NIST SP 800-53 (Control SI-2), PCI-DSS 4.0, and DORA enforce strict timelines for critical and high-severity issues. When 9.0+ CVSS scores arrive in weekly batches, security and platform leads spend more time writing risk-acceptance waivers than hardening production architecture. Can internal IT teams keep up with patching and push innovation? The short answer is no . Enterprise development exists to deliver business value: ship differentiated features, enhance platform reliability, and expand market share. Yet today’s software supply…
