articles.title: US tech jobs grow in a ‘low-hire, low-fire’ market
articles.content: Tech jobs grew in October, and the holiday season will provide a boost in an otherwise “low-hire, low-fire” market, data released by research firms showed. The tech industry added 7,200 jobs, and tech jobs across all industries grew by 26,000 in October, according to CompTIA , which studied numbers released by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics. The BLS said the US added 165,000 jobs overall in October. Job gains were in tech manufacturing, IT services, and software. IT unemployment was at 2.8%, lower than the national average of 4.1%. Seasonal hiring to provide a boost A separate study by Challenger, Gray & Christmas said seasonal jobs from Amazon — which announced plans to hire 300,000 workers — will boost hiring in the technology sector. “Amazon’s 300,000 seasonal hires account for nearly all of the 300,252 Technology hiring plans announced in October,” the research firm said. Amazon’s seasonal jobs will largely be in warehousing and e-commerce fulfillment. The research firm considers them tech jobs, as the company is in the tech sector. The hiring is largely short-term, seasonal work, and “companies want the flexibility to meet holiday demand without adding permanent headcount,” Challenger said. Warehouse associate postings are up 13% from a year ago and have grown for three straight months as employers gear up for the seasonal rush, said Ger Doyle , regional president for North America at ManpowerGroup, a staffing and recruitment agency. “Despite that growth, warehouse postings year-to-date are still running slightly behind 2025’s pace, pointing to a recovery in demand rather than a new high,” Doyle said. Growth in jobs — for some The latest numbers reflect a strong labor market, which is encouraging, Doyle said. But gains are still concentrated in areas such as engineering, manufacturing, and logistics, specifically related to data centers, semiconductors, and infrastructure, he said. “For workers, job openings aren’t necessarily translating into hiring, and the jobs that are growing aren’t always where the people looking for work are,” Doyle said. Even though demand is starting to improve, it still isn’t easy for people to find work or feel better off, Doyle said. “What we’re watching now is whether this improvement turns into faster, broader hiring and wages start to regain ground against inflation,” Doyle said. Tech job cuts in October totaled 5,576, which is the lowest of the year, according to Challenger, Gray & Christmas. “Even so, the sector leads all industries with 171,501 cuts through October, up 21% from the 141,159 announced in the same period last year,” Challenger said. The technology sector accounts for 28% of job cuts in 2026, the firm said. A hefty job reduction may be looming, with Microsoft offering voluntary exits to 60,000 employees. Challenger will record those numbers depending on the number of employees accepting the offers or Microsoft’s target. What job listings say Despite what research firms called a slow hiring environment, the number of new IT job listings reached 290,892 in October, up 22.2% from a year ago, according to CompTIA. Job listings for AI skills across sectors reached 366,322 in October, growing by 6.2% from September. According to the Indeed hiring tracker , AI appeared in 7.3% of its job listings on September 30, doubling from the same day last year. Job postings tied to data centers are up 52% year-over-year, while semiconductor demand is up 92%, said Kye Mitchell , president of Experis North America, which is owned by ManpowerGroup. More than half of data center operators are struggling to find qualified workers, which may include engineers, technical workers, and IT talent, Mitchell said. But hiring may change after US voters nationwide voted to slow down data center development during the November midterm election. Data center projects could face more scrutiny around energy, infrastructure costs, and location at a time when employers are already competing for specialized…

articles.title: How advertising machines broke the attention economy
articles.content: In 2016, TV advertising was in trouble. People were canceling their cable subscriptions by the millions, ratings were slipping, and advertisers were pouring billions of dollars into digital platforms that promised bigger audiences than TV at a much lower cost. That April, Buzzfeed broadcast a live stream of two staffers in white coats and safety goggles wrapping rubber bands around a watermelon. The tension mounted as the rubber bands piled up, one at a time, hundreds and hundreds of them, squeezing the watermelon until it began to buckle. When it finally burst, sending pulp flying and its hosts shrieking, the live stream had been viewed more than 3 million times. CNBC called it the future of television. Except it wasn’t. There was no way to tell how much of the audience actually watched the spectacle, or only watched it for a few seconds. The video may have simply run on autoplay as they scrolled past. But for advertisers, every three-second “view” counted as an impression, which was the industry’s basic unit of value. Advertising had always been the business of attention. But attention is finite. There are only 24 hours in a day, and people can look at only so many things at once. But the algorithms that controlled digital advertising weren’t built to reflect that reality. They were given an incentive: maximize ad revenue. So they learned to produce and promote whatever generated the most impressions. An impression was counted each time an ad, or the content around it, appeared on a screen for a few seconds, whether or not anyone actually noticed it. When the algorithms ran short of real attention to sell, they expanded into areas that required no attention at all: intercepting demand that already existed and claiming credit for purchases people would have made anyway. That set off a snowball effect. The supply of ad inventory exploded. The result was a flood of cheap, low-quality impressions—a subprime market for human attention. As supply soared, prices fell for every seller of advertising. Never mind that TV commercials were graded differently. Scrolling past an exploding watermelon on your phone was treated the same way as watching every minute of a prime-time drama or a World Series game. A vicious cycle As television was forced to compete on digital’s terms, networks ran more minutes of advertising, which made the viewing experience worse and probably played a role in pushing even more viewers toward streaming and ad-free platforms. It was a vicious cycle. The less attention was worth, the more “impressions” the industry had to manufacture to make up the difference. As traditional TV ads lost value, some networks experimented with cutting ad loads and rethinking the commercial break altogether. At the time, Jonathan was in charge of advertising at Fox Networks Group, and we experimented with a bunch of new formats: six-second spots, premium slots at the start and end of commercial breaks and even single-sponsor streams with minimal interruptions. Other networks pursued their own versions of the same idea, promising viewers fewer, better ads and offering advertisers more engaged audiences. These new formats provided a better value exchange for viewers’ attention. But they were a hard sell. Buyers asked why six seconds should cost more than 30. The real estate and retail industries valued placement and scarcity, but when it came to the advertising market, brands wanted volume. Real change required advertisers to let their agencies take risks and most wouldn’t do it. A decade later, the stakes are even higher. There are still only 24 hours in a day, but artificial intelligence can now generate an unlimited supply of content. Feeds are filling up with AI-generated videos, and platforms are automating every step of advertising, from writing an ad to targeting the audience to placing the buy. There are now even ads inside AI assistants. ChatGPT says it’s on track to generate $1 billion in annual ad revenue , and more than…

articles.title: A New Dawn in the Cloud: ‘Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV’ Is Coming to GeForce NOW
articles.content: Rally the ranks this GFN Thursday. Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV is coming to GeForce NOW , allowing players to experience the battle for Kronus through cloud gaming. There’s more on the horizon, with NVIDIA DLSS 5 technology coming to War Thunder and Where Winds Meet . Meanwhile, Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen brings new tales and encounters, alongside 10 games joining the GeForce NOW library this week. Kronus Calls for Reinforcements Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV , developed by KING Art Games and published by Deep Silver, is coming to GeForce NOW. Launching on Steam Thursday, Dec. 3, the real-time strategy game returns to the series’ roots with large-scale battles, base building and a renewed fight for planet Kronus. Command the Space Marines, Orks, Necrons or the Adeptus Mechanicus, which makes their series debut. Build a base, secure resources and customize squads to the conflict across more than 70 campaign missions, playable solo or in co-op mode. The Last Stand, Skirmish and multiplayer modes offer more ways to put tactics to the test. GeForce NOW will bring the action to supported PCs, Macs, handhelds and other devices, with game downloads and updates handled in the cloud. Save the storage space for everyday essentials and planning for the next offensive. Wishlist the game on Steam , and stay tuned to GFN Thursday to prepare for launch. DLSS 5 Keeps on Coming NVIDIA DLSS 5 continues to evolve, with Gaijin Entertainment’s War Thunder and Everstone Studio’s Where Winds Meet next to receive support for the technology with the 3D-Guided Neural Rendering feature. Arriving in mid-November, War Thunder ’s Eagle’s Shadow major update adds DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, dozens of new planes, ships and tanks, along with cluster bombs for planes and visual-effects enhancements increasing the realism and dynamism of battle. In Where Winds Meet , DLSS support arrives Monday, Nov. 23, enhancing the environments and characters of its wuxia open-world action role-playing game. Both titles will use the latest DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering model, released in October, which doubles model performance compared with the previous version. Since its initial announcement in March, model performance has improved tenfold, bringing the technology to more gamers, including GeForce NOW Ultimate members streaming with GeForce RTX 5080 cloud rigs. Get a closer look at the DLSS updates and find more details . A New Tale for the Arisen Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is streaming on GeForce NOW, expanding the deep, explorable fantasy world of Dragon’s Dogma 2 with new tales and encounters. Travel to the long-abandoned region of Norgan, join the enigmatic Eir and uncover the secrets of the undying Fallen Dragon. Unearth forgotten relics to unlock powerful weapons and skills, take on Lost Rites’ 12 dungeon challenges and explore new hairstyles and tattoos for Arisen and Pawn customization. Delicious in Dungeon also arrives in the world of Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen with a special collaboration. GeForce NOW keeps all the new downloadable content available across supported devices — without a single download claiming local storage on a gamer’s hardware of choice. In addition, members can look for the following games joining the GeForce NOW library this week: Worst Class Ever (New release on Steam , Nov. 9) Ashes of the Singularity II (New release on Steam , Nov. 10) Cyberpunk 2077 ( Xbox Play Anywhere, new release on Battle.net , Nov. 10) DreamWorks Shrek 2 Remastered (New release on Steam , Nov. 10) Warhammer Survivors (New release on Steam and Xbox , available on Game Pass, Nov. 10) Main Sequence (New release on Steam , Nov. 12) Deadly Days: Roadtrip ( Steam ) GeForce 8800 GTX – 20 Years of a Legend ( Steam , Ultimate members) Graveyard Keeper ( Steam ) Tape to Tape ( Steam ) Also this week, Ultimate members can take a trip back to 2006 with GeForce 8800 GTX – 20 Years of a Legend , a playable demo celebrating the iconic GPU’s…

articles.title: Corsair HX1000i Shift Crystal power supply review: 1000W Platinum efficiency with an eye-catching transparent aesthetic
articles.content: Corsair needs very little introduction to anyone who has built a PC over the past two decades. Founded in California in 1994 as a manufacturer of memory modules, the company has since grown into one of the largest brands in the PC component and peripheral market, with a catalog that covers cases, cooling, keyboards, mice, streaming gear, and of course, power supplies. Corsair entered the PSU market in the second half of the 2000s and built its reputation there by choosing its OEM partners carefully rather than manufacturing in-house. Channel Well Technology (CWT) has been one of the most important of these partners, producing a large portion of the RMx and HXi units over the years. The HXi series in particular has long been Corsair's high-end, digitally monitored family, positioned just below the flagship AX models. We take a closer look at the HX1000i Shift Crystal to see if it deserves a spot in our best power supplies list. The HX1000i Shift Crystal is a bit of an odd bird, and Corsair is clearly fine with that. First shown at Computex 2026 and launching on November 12th, it combines the side-mounted connector layout of the SHIFT models with the digital HXi platform, and then wraps everything in a chassis with clear polycarbonate panels on three sides, turning the internals of the PSU into a part of the build's aesthetics. Beneath the show, the platform is built by CWT. It holds a Cybenetics Platinum certification at both 115 VAC and 230 VAC, and it is fully compliant with the ATX 3.1 and PCIe 5.1 design guides. It also integrates an iCUE LINK System Hub and Corsair's PinProtect+ per-pin current monitoring for the native 12V-2x6 connector. The 1000W model that we are reviewing today is rated to deliver its full power output continuously at ambient temperatures up to 50°C and comes with a ten-year warranty. Inside the box, we found the AC power cord, four mounting screws, a handful of black cable ties, and a leaflet with safety and compliance information. There are no Velcro straps, no cable combs beyond those already on the cables, and no other accessories of any kind. It is not a deal breaker by any means, but a premium unit like this that is focused on aesthetics could have been a little more generous in this department. articles.title: See what AI looks like in production at Microsoft Ignite
articles.content: If you’re deciding which AI pilots to move into production, Microsoft’s Satya Nadella and Judson Althoff’s opening keynote at Microsoft Ignite will show you where the company is taking the tools you’ll use to build and run those agents. They take the stage at 10 a.m. Pacific on Tuesday, November 17. After the opening keynote, you can experience how customers put AI into production at scale, see where Microsoft is taking the tools those customers use, and compare notes with industry colleagues already doing the work. The breakout sessions (and hallway networking) offer the opportunity to double-click into results after an actual deployment. With the rapid advancement of AI tools and resources, the best playbook is often the one your peers have already tested. Microsoft Ignite gives leaders a place to compare deployment strategies and lessons learned face to face, with organizations just getting started and others already getting results from AI in production. Microsoft tells The New Stack that over four days, more than 100 organizations will take the stage across keynotes, breakout sessions and theater stages. Microsoft tells The New Stack that over four days, more than 100 organizations will take the stage across keynotes, breakout sessions and theater stages. The organizations span AI startups such as Replit and Harvey, financial firms including Morgan Stanley and BNY, and companies such as Toyota and Siemens. If you’re choosing a first project (or deciding which pilot deserves more budget), the range at Ignite should give you a chance to gauge how teams with different goals are making those same decisions you’re facing. How Microsoft AI solutions work together Microsoft calls its approach Frontier Transformation . It starts with what people want to accomplish, the information AI agents need to help them, and finally, the controls an organization needs once AI is in use. For employees, Microsoft 365 Copilot puts AI into tools they already use, including Teams and Word. Microsoft Fabric brings business data and analytics together, and Microsoft IQ gives Copilot and agents context, pulling from in-house data, workplace activity, documents, and the web. Developers can use GitHub and GitHub Copilot to write and review code, then use Microsoft Foundry to build, test, and deploy agents on Azure infrastructure . Finally, Agent 365 gives IT teams a place to see which agents are running, monitor their activity, and set policies. Customer stories will also be a big part of each of the four innovation sessions. Where should your AI actually run? Mark Russinovich and Pavan Davuluri will lead “AI Infrastructure From Cloud to Edge,” with examples of Microsoft using its own tech as “Customer Zero” (what Microsoft calls its high-stakes version of dogfooding). PricewaterhouseCoopers will appear in person, and OpenAI, Adobe, and Replit will share featured videos in this session. If you’re deciding what to run in Azure vs. closer to users, this session will offer the insight you need. Microsoft reports that more than 40,000 people at Lilly use Copilot How do you get people using agents in their everyday work? Lilly’s Bryce Williams is scheduled to join Microsoft’s Jacob Andreou in person for “Expanding What’s Possible: How AI Is Redesigning Work.” Microsoft reports that more than 40,000 people at Lilly use Copilot, and that more than 150 agents support work across research, clinical trials, and operations. If your team is rolling out Copilot, Lilly will showcase what helped its teams adopt it at scale. How do you ensure your agents are working from the right information? In “Harnessing Your IQ With a Continuously Improving Agent Platform,” Arun Ulag and Jay Parikh will look at how agents use company data and knowledge, with planned spotlights on AEMO and NTT Data. You’ll hear how teams decide what an agent should be able to see and…

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns in the wake of multiple affairs, Chinese spy allegations
articles.content: Nvidia’s board of directors has confirmed today that Jensen Huang has resigned as the company's CEO. The news follows revelations that Huang had been involved in not one but two extramarital affairs, one with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, and another with his direct report, Nvidia’s VP of health care, Kimberly Powell. "NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately," the board stated. "Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates." In recent weeks, stories have come to light alleging that Huang was involved in an overly familiar relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence agencies suspect may be a Chinese intelligence asset. It was reported that the AI GPU giant’s CEO may have been the target of a spy plot — Megaspeed is under investigatio n for its involvement in the smuggling of $2 billion worth of export-controlled AI GPUs into China. Nvidia shares plunged more than 10 percent in early market trading following the news, and are now down more than 23% in the last month. Over the weekend, Jensen Huang admitted that he had been unfaithful to his wife and issued a company-wide apology. Separately, Nvidia’s Board of Directors launched an independent investigation into reports that Huang’s entanglement may be a matter of national security, given his role in the global AI revolution. Colette Kress has been Nvidia's Executive Vice President and CFO since September 2013; prior to that, she spent 25 years at Cisco and Microsoft, among others. Just a couple of days later, a second bombshell report emerged claiming that Jensen Huang was also romantically involved with Powell , one of his direct reports at the company. Reports indicate the affair was known within the company, and that the two were even filmed being affectionate in a San Jose hotel at Nvidia GTC. Security allegedly sequestered a bystander who filmed the interaction on camera and made the person an offer to sign a nondisclosure agreement. Nvidia also announced that Harvey C. Jones will serve as the company's first-ever Chair of the Board; he has previously served as CEO and Executive Chairman of Synopsys.

articles.title: The Download: COP31’s climate challenge and the quest for immortality
articles.content: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. What to know about this year’s UN climate talks Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists have gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the annual UN climate talks. But this year’s negotiations are taking place against a particularly tense geopolitical backdrop, as the world falls further behind the Paris Agreement’s goals. Energy prices are soaring, and there are big questions about how countries will tackle the climate crisis. Expect a lot of back and forth on fossil fuels and climate finance, and whether negotiators can agree on meaningful action. Here’s what you need to know about COP31 . —Casey Crownhart This story is from The Spark, our weekly climate tech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday. MIT Technology Review’s latest Roundtables event explores their ideas, from gradual brain replacement to uploading memories to the cloud. articles.title: Noctua brings space-grade carbon nanotube thermal pad to AMD AM5 and AM4 processors
articles.content: Austrian cooling outfit Noctua is officially rolling its new NT-CP1 AM5/4 Carbice carbon nanotube thermal pad for AMD AM4 and AM5 processors into the retail market. After announcing its partnership with advanced nanotechnology company Carbice back in June 2026, the premium thermal pad can now be purchased for $24.95 in the US and €24.95 in the European region. Grab the Noctua NT-CP1 AM5/4 Carbice carbon nanotube thermal pad on Amazon Conventional thermal pastes and most thermal pads gradually lose performance over time due to pump-out, delamination, cracking, and other forms of degradation. However, Noctua says that its new NT-CP1 thermal pad takes a different approach. It makes use of Carbice's vertically-aligned carbon nanotube technology, originally developed for high thermal reliability in aerospace systems. The carbon nanotubes gradually conform to microscopic imperfections of a CPU’s IHS over hundreds to thousands of thermal cycles. This allows heat transfer performance to improve during the initial activation period rather than gradually deteriorating. The thermal pad can also maintain stable, maintenance-free performance for years once the initial activation phase is complete. Thus, making it a suitable option for users who want consistent thermal performance without having to periodically replace degraded thermal paste. "Carbice pads offer a unique combination of ultimate performance stability and convenient installation. This makes the NT-CP1 the perfect choice for everyone who’s looking for a thermal pad that’s super easy to apply and never needs to be replaced," said Noctua CEO Roland Mossig in a press note. Unlike conventional carbon or graphite-based thermal pads, which can be brittle, slippery, and electrically conductive, the NT-CP1 features an aluminum backbone sandwiched between layers of carbon nanotubes. The surface is also protected by a nanoscale polymer coating, which Noctua says makes the pad more robust, easier to handle, and less likely to move during installation. The company recommends a simple peel, press, and peel installation process, while the slightly tacky coating helps keep the pad in place and offers electrical insulation as long as the polymer layer remains intact. With an ultra-thin 90µm profile and precut 33x33mm size, the thermal pad fits both AM5 and AM4 socket processors. Noctua also highlights its manufacturing process, noting that the pad is produced in the US using recycled aluminum and waste carbon gas to grow the carbon nanotubes. The company claims that its manufacturing process is more energy-efficient compared to conventional graphite and graphene-based pads, while the aluminum structure allows the product to be recycled through standard aluminum recycling channels.

articles.title: Suspected Chinese spy at center of Jensen Huang affair surfaces in Beijing
articles.content: Alice Huang, the person allegedly involved in an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, has reportedly surfaced in Beijing, marking the first sighting of the Megaspeed executive since the scandal broke out. According to Bloomberg , it’s unclear when the suspected Chinese spy arrived in the capital or why she’s in the area, but she was last spotted leaving Singapore for Shanghai in 2025 after she was detained and questioned during the city-state’s investigation into the $2-billion smuggling case involving Megaspeed. The Nvidia CEO is now under intense scrutiny after the revelation of his indiscretion with the Megaspeed executive, with Congress threatening to issue a subpoena if he does not respond to their invitation to “a joint, closed-door briefing” with the heads of the House committees on China, Foreign Affairs, and Intelligence. The FBI is also looking into the relationship between the head of the largest AI hardware company in the world and a person suspected of helping sanctioned Chinese companies secure hundreds of thousands of banned H100 and H200 chips . Overnight, a second bombshell report claims that Jensen Huang was also involved in an extramarital affair with Nvidia's VP of health care, Kimberly Powell . Although the Chinese embassy in Washington has denied any links to Alice Huang, calling it nothing but “groundless smears and slanders” against Beijing, there is speculation that she’s under the control of the Ministry of State Security (MSS), which is the primary agency that handles China’s foreign intelligence and counterintelligence operations. The U.S. intelligence community suggests that she may be passing on information to the MSS, but it remains unclear if she was specifically tasked by Chinese intelligence to target Jensen Huang or if they were only leveraging her relationship with the Nvidia chief to get insights into the U.S. AI industry. A deeper investigation into Alice Huang, known by her Chinese name as Huang Le, revealed that she supposedly worked in media before jumping into banking and finance. The Wall Street Journal reports that it’s unclear when she met her husband, Kang Wei, but the couple ran a private equity and investment management firm called Shanghai Hexi in 2016. This allowed the couple to invest in companies across industries, including gaming, pharmaceuticals, and, eventually, data centers and cloud computing. The couple is known for riding trends and isn’t a stranger to scandals. Their firm, Shanghai Hexi, invested in gaming companies in the 2010s, especially when mobile gaming started to boom across the world, while Chinese regulators fined Kang and the company in 2018 for disclosure failures and other violations while it was in the midst of a takeover battle for a corporation. Kang’s moves in the gaming industry are what allowed him to meet Jensen Huang, which eventually led to a close relationship between the couple and the Nvidia chief. Sources told the WSJ that Kang apparently accepted Alice and Jensen’s extra-marital relationship, even sometimes jokingly telling people that she was Jensen’s “personal assistant.” It seems that the couple is used to leveraging their relationships to gain business advantage, and with investments in AI data centers expected to hit $32 trillion by 2050 , Alice Huang’s “close” relationship with Jensen Huang put Shanghai Hexi in an excellent position to take advantage of the trend through Megaspeed and make big money. And with U.S. sanctions making it harder for competitors to acquire Nvidia chips, it appears that their access has turned into a gold mine for the company. But whether Alice Huang acted solely out of business interest with the supposed procurement of Nvidia chips or was leveraged by Chinese authorities to import these chips, the fact remains that $7.5 billion worth of banned chips reportedly made their way into China despite Washington’s efforts.

articles.title: Google Deepmind shifts genomics AI from bulk tissue predictions to single cell type resolution with AlphaGenome 2
articles.content: Google Deepmind has unveiled AlphaGenome 2, an AI model that analyzes genetic variants for individual cell types rather than across bulk tissue. Trained on more than 107 million cell profiles, it identifies nearly twice as many disease-relevant gene changes as its predecessor. The model is available for noncommercial research through an API and is set to be integrated into Google's agentic platform Antigravity. articles.title: How Founders Can Reduce Platform Risk Before It Threatens Growth
articles.content: By Yakov Filippenko One day, I woke up to a notice that our app had been removed from Apple’s App Store. For the next month or so, we racked our brains trying to find out why. We even reached out to our internal contacts, only for them to tell us that helping us could put their jobs at risk. Nothing seemed to work. For years, the App Store’s unwritten contract seemed simple. As long as you followed the guidelines, your storefront would remain available. Then a removal notice arrives, and you wonder whether your business can survive. In 2025, Apple removed 166,899 apps and reported just 423 restorations after appeals. As we learned, being caught in it feels like watching your business collapse, with no guarantee of recovery. It’s not all bad news, though. We survived, and this episode taught me that platform dependency is ultimately infrastructure risk. As founders, we prepare for cloud outages and payment failures, but losing access to the platform that brings us customers deserves the same attention. Fortunately, we were prepared, and this is how you can be, too. Understand what a removal can take away Yakov Filippenko, founder and CEO at Intch. First, prospective customers can no longer download your app. Then, paying subscribers flood support with a more damaging question. “The app is gone. Are you a scam?” The bloodshed continues as existing users replace their phones and can’t reinstall the app, eroding your customer base. Financially, Apple immediately freezes funds from the previous three months and turns off recurring subscriptions. For a subscription-dependent company, this can send its monthly recurring revenue to zero. Before spending another cent on acquisition, consider what would happen to those customers if your app disappeared tomorrow. Could they still use your product and continue paying you? If the answer is no, every new customer makes your business more dependent on a platform decision you cannot control. Don’t make an appeal your contingency plan Cal AI , reportedly generating $100,000 daily, was pulled without warning and later reappeared. But its reinstatement tells you little about how long your business might wait. In Intch ’s case, the explanation was so generic it told us nothing. We had 30 days to appeal, but the process ended with a canned rejection. Your appeal may succeed, but your business must operate while you wait. Preparing in advance lets you keep going, whatever the outcome. Build the alternative before you need it Our experience was grueling, but fortunately, two years earlier we had decoupled from the App Store by building a web version and making it our primary payment channel. It also let us ship updates 10 times a day while escaping Apple’s predatory commissions. We weren’t the only ones. Pavel Durov , founder of Telegram , has also promoted web access to bypass store restrictions and potential censorship. The lesson is straightforward. Customers need a working alternative before access disappears. Building one only after removal leaves the business exposed while the team races to replace its storefront. We initially feared the user experience would suffer, but that concern proved unfounded. After the removal, every key metric fully recovered. If you share this concern, test it while your app is still available to see whether customers can use and pay for the web version before they must rely on it. Include platform exposure in growth decisions Most founders see the App Store as a distribution channel, but rarely account for how much control it gives Apple over their business. Before investing more in growth, examine how much revenue depends on continued access and what would survive a removal. Know how long the company could survive an unanswered appeal. Investors should ask those questions too, because a growing subscription base deserves closer scrutiny when a single platform decision can interrupt its revenue. That exposure belongs in funding and valuation…

articles.title: VCs Are Still Chasing Protein, Even As Fake Meat Falls Out Of Favor
articles.content: Macronutrients don’t have popularity contests. But if they did, protein would surely be this era’s winner. For everything from sodas to snack bars to pasta, it’s now standard practice for food and drink makers to play up protein content whenever feasible. While we may cut carbs and fret over fat, most of us are still keen on protein. Startups and their backers have been riding this trend too. Over the past decade, investors have poured billions into upstarts promising cheaper, tastier and more sustainable ways to meet our protein quotas. Unfortunately, many of their earlier bets have fared poorly. Vast sums poured into lab-grown meat several years ago, for instance, have so far failed to produce a success story. Former high-flying plant-based meat startups Beyond (now public) and Impossible Foods have seen their valuations wither. Others have shuttered. In response, more recent startup investment has shifted away from meat substitutes and toward stuffing more protein into other packaged foods and drinks. It’s a fad that’s obvious on supermarket shelves, where startups and established brands alike relentlessly tout the added protein in their noodles, pancakes, cereals, energy bars, popcorn and so on. Deal flow looks robust In startup circles, protein-related investment looks tiny in comparison to the billions bet on AI. Deal flow, however, remains fairly robust, with Crunchbase identifying a few dozen protein-focused startups funded in the past year. Moreover, some of these rounds are quite sizable, like a $250 million September Series B for Medici Brands , maker of David Protein snack bars. To illustrate, we used Crunchbase data to put together sample sets of recently-funded protein-focused companies across several themes. These include packaged foods, drinks, ingredients and processes, and animal feed. Protein snacks and packaged foods Snacks and packaged foods look like the largest fundraisers among protein startups, securing hundreds of millions in the past year. For a sense of who’s raising, we put together a list of seven recently funded brands that are finding their way to store shelves. The bulk of recent funding went to the aforementioned parent of David Protein. That brand, in addition to churning sweet-flavored bars with a protein content to rival cod , has been expanding into ice cream and milkshakes. Wilde Brands , which makes crackers from chicken breasts, has also proven popular with investors, pulling in $40 million last month. Among early-stage startups, meanwhile, Frozen One has been off to a brisk start, raising over $8 million for a line of high-protein ice creams now selling at Target . Protein drinks Startups and investors are also catering to people who want their high-protein diet in drinkable form. To illustrate, we put together six recently funded examples below. Ripple Foods , which makes a vegan milk using pea protein, is the highest historical funding recipient, raising over $300 million in its 12-year-history, even though it hasn’t officially joined the unicorn club. Clear protein drinks are also increasingly a thing, with multiple startups including protein soda brand Juuz and sports drink purveyor Protein2o . Precision fermentation and plant protein ingredients Quite a few funded startups are focused more on novel, protein-rich ingredients rather than their own branded retail lineup. In many cases, they’re using precision fermentation to deliver. We put together seven examples below. The Every Co. , which makes animal-free egg white proteins through fermentation, is the biggest funding recipient and one of the older names on our list. It’s raised nearly $300 million in the past 10 years, including a $55 million round a year ago. articles.title: Bending Spoons is buying up the internet. Can its business model last?
articles.content: Bending Spoons has already acquired some of the internet’s most recognizable software brands. And it has identified more than 1,000 others it could potentially acquire. The Milan-based company, whose portfolio includes Evernote, WeTransfer, Vimeo, AOL, and Eventbrite, disclosed the figure in its IPO prospectus . Together, those potential targets generated nearly $400 billion in estimated revenue in 2025. Bending Spoons has hardly slowed down since its stock market debut in July. It has completed acquisitions of Airtable and Miro, and in October, Berkshire Hathaway invested another $330 million , bringing its ownership stake to 4%. Its business model— buy an established product with paying customers, reorganize the company, reduce costs, improve the technology, and use the profits to pursue more acquisitions—is attracting attention across the software industry. And the results have generally been impressive. But so have the job cuts. As AI makes software cheaper to develop and maintain, Bending Spoons may now be establishing a new model for an industry accustomed to prioritizing growth over profitability. WHY BUYING OLD SOFTWARE MAKES FINANCIAL SENSE Building a successful software business is expensive. A company could spend years developing a product, attracting customers, and trying to persuade them to pay for it with no guarantee it will succeed. Buying an established business, however, reduces some of that uncertainty. “From an investor’s perspective, the fundamental advantage is that you’re buying proven behavior rather than financing the search for it,” says Vince Molinari, a financial services expert and founder and CEO of Fintech Media Group. An established product already has customers, revenue, brand recognition, and a distribution network. For an acquirer, the opportunity often lies in improving how the business operates. Molinari places particular importance on customer retention. A company with loyal subscribers and inefficient operations may be more attractive than a fast-growing business whose customers regularly leave. “Revenue tells you what customers paid yesterday. Retention helps tell you whether they’ll still be paying tomorrow,” he tells Fast Company . Bending Spoons’ second-quarter results illustrate the appeal. Revenue rose 126% from a year earlier to $704 million, while operating income increased 139% to $240 million. But acquisitions accounted for most of the revenue growth. Looking at its businesses without the extra revenue added by acquisitions, growth was just 3%. The figures show how heavily the company’s expansion still depends on buying businesses, rather than growing revenue from the ones it owns. “The next billion-dollar opportunity doesn’t necessarily start with the next big idea,” says Nadja Atwal, an international business adviser. “Sometimes it starts with recognizing that someone else’s old big idea still has plenty of life left in it.” THE COST OF MAKING SOFTWARE MORE PROFITABLE Bending Spoons is unusually willing to make sweeping changes after an acquisition. Its IPO filing disclosed that AOL, Eventbrite, and Vimeo collectively brought approximately 1,830 full-time-equivalent employees into the company. According to the filing, Bending Spoons planned to retain only a few hundred of those employees after restructuring the businesses. The scale of such restructuring has attracted much criticism, but Vimeo offers an example of how Bending Spoons believes its approach can improve acquired products. At Vimeo, Bending Spoons reported more than 30 product improvements during the second quarter, alongside a roughly 90% reduction in system-stability incidents compared with pre-acquisition levels. Uploads and searches also became at least 30% faster, according to the company. These are encouraging results, although they are company-reported figures. Improvements in speed and reliability don’t necessarily tell us how customers feel about pricing, support, or the product’s direction. Matteo…

articles.title: Claris Harbor could turn Mac fleets into on-prem AI servers
articles.content: It feels quite appropriate that one of Apple’s more interesting AI deployments may not come from the company itself, but from its more business-focused subsidiary, Claris, still better known to many as FileMaker. What we know is limited: It intends to release an app that uses Apple Silicon Macs to create a private AI server. What Claris is promising The company, famous for its database software for the enterprise, has initiated a private preview of what sounds — at least on the surface — like something worth watching for enterprise users seeking to achieve AI insights from their data. The product is called Claris Harbor, and the company says it “turns the Apple silicon computers you own into a private AI server.” To achieve this, Harbor leans steeply into the powerful performance packed inside Apple Silicon : “Set up an endpoint in minutes on a single Mac.” It also makes use of the existing features of Macs that have already made them so popular among people deploying OpenClaw. “When you want to run larger models, connect multiple machines over Thunderbolt 5 to pool unified memory on hardware you control,” Claris said. It also says you can set up an endpoint on a single Mac — one of your Macs becomes an AI server for everyone else . Your Macs. Your AI Put this together and you have an Apple solution built around the part of the company with extensive enterprise and database experience that offers one of the emerging holy grails of business-class AI — powerful, scalable AI that can work on confidential and protected data on-premises, on-device, and in confidence. “Data and prompts stay strictly within your physical Mac hardware,” the company promised. While Claris doesn’t claim it, it’s not hard to imagine those banks of Macs already deployed in business being used as AI clusters overnight before returning to normal business use in the morning. That’s what the ability to connect multiple machines makes possible — though it’s not quite what Claris claims. Little more is known about the solution at this point. The company has opened a mailing list to keep potential customers informed, promising to provide early access to the new private AI server as it is built. Why Claris, and why now? I like the approach to this. Claris has been a consistently profitable entity for Apple. At one point in the history of the company, it was this part of its operation that kept the rest of the firm afloat. It has extensive experience in both data and enterprise and may therefore be the best part of the Apple machine from which to disseminate a wholly Apple approach to local AI. It comes at a good time. Frontier AI has hit a wall of colossal spending combined with relatively feeble returns, even as enterprise customers rapidly recognize the need to protect their data. Enterprise interest in local AI has surged. Businesses are already moving beyond the experimental cloud-only approach, navigating toward deployments guided by the need to control costs, protect data, and provide predictable governance. Deloitte’s State of AI in the Enterprise report, released last month, tells us that 74% of enterprises now prioritize data residency and in-region compute. If, as seems likely, Harbor is designed to integrate tightly with FileMaker databases, that opens a potential market of up to 1.3 million existing FileMaker users for this Apple approach to AI. Claris also has a community of over 30,000 developers, and it would be in keeping with FileMaker’s approach to relational database development for Harbor to be configurable in some way, making it a flexible solution for business users. We shall wait and see the extent to which that potential is realized as Harbor heads toward opening. What we don’t know yet Claris will have to answer some hard questions to build strong momentum once its new solution ships. Enterprise purchasers will want to know what AI models it runs and will be curious about the performance Thunderbolt 5 pooling provides when it comes to…

articles.title: Tim Peters, Python User #2 and Prolific Contributor, Dies At 74
articles.content: Tim Peters, one of Python's earliest and most influential contributors, died on July 15 at age 74. Known as Python's second real user, Peters created the Zen of Python and Timsort sorting algorithm while contributing to numerous core components. He also served as a Python Software Foundation director from 2001 to 2014. Adafruit remembers Peters in a blog post: He's best known for the Zen of Python, PEP 20, still printed by typing import this. In 2002, he gave Python Timsort, the sorting algorithm he designed for lists, later adopted by Java and Android. He also polished the cyclic garbage collector and the pymalloc allocator, worked on the dict implementation, the float object, the math module and Karatsuba multiplication in longobject, and wrote the first version of doctest, plus difflib, pickletools and tabnanny. He was a director of the Python Software Foundation from 2001 to 2014. Before Python, he wrote compilers at Cray Research and speech-to-text software at Dragon Systems. The thread is full of recollections from core developers about his patient, detailed answers on the mailing lists, signed with his trademark . Python creator Guido van Rossum also paid tribute to Peters in a post on discuss.python.org, writing: "It's hard to overestimate Tim's influence on Python. He's probably best known for writing the Zen of Python (PEP 20), but to me he was a mentor and language co-designer long before that..." Further discussions can be found on Hacker News and Reddit. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Should You Actually Add AI To That? A Four-Question Audit For Product Teams
articles.content: A product team at a large health insurer wants to add AI that writes the full written determination for benefits appeals specialists. The technology works as specified. However, the specialists stop using it, and the ones who keep using it take longer on each case than the ones who ignore it. A short evaluation with the specialists surfaces the problem fast: reading an AI-written determination carefully enough to sign it takes about as long as writing one, and the specialist also has to check for mistakes they would never have made themselves. The feature adds work to a task these people had already mastered. Rescoping the release fixes it. A second version surfaces the policy provisions and prior decisions relevant to each appeal and leaves the writing to the specialist. The search step disappears, review time drops, and the part of the job the specialist is good at stays where it was. The technology is identical in both versions, and the difference is which part of the task the AI handles. Finding The Break-even Line Every interface change costs the user something before it pays anything back. They have to rebuild their picture of how the tool works, learn where things are now, and decide how far to trust what the AI hands them. Nelson Cowan’s review of working memory research (2001) put the limit at about four items held in mind at once. All three of those jobs draw on the same small supply. An AI feature in an enterprise software setting requires more from the user than a redesigned menu, because it changes what they do all day. Hand the synthesis to an AI and the user becomes a checker. Give it the recommendation too, and the job shrinks to signing off. Either change costs user attention, and for people whose training is their standing at work, either one can feel like a demotion. For example, in one study, Sophia Ackerhans (2025) and colleagues found that physicians asked to sign AI-assisted decisions reported a more serious threat to their professional identity, and explanations of the AI’s reasoning raised both trust and that threat together. An AI feature earns its place when what it returns beats what it costs the user to adjust, for one user doing one task. We can call that the break-even line . Returns to users come in three forms: Effort the feature removes, Errors it catches that the person would have missed, and Consistency across people doing the same work. For example, an AI-powered fraud screening tool shows the errors-caught form at work, since the analyst reviews flags they would never have raised themselves, which costs attention, and the catch rate pays for it. That puts the feature above the break-even line. Four questions can help your team locate the break-even line before design work starts. Each one produces a design condition the brief can act on. These questions do not replace the build decision. Funding, strategy, and existing commitments all weigh on that, and four questions cannot see any of it. Run through all four questions together , since no single question settles the issue alone. Do it while the feature is still a proposal, before anyone sinks weeks into design. You will also need at least one person who does the task for a living, such as a loan officer, analyst, or benefits specialist. They do not have to sit in the roadmap meeting, and a short conversation tells you where the mental effort actually sits and whether the feature would help or add work. Question 1: Does This Reduce The Total Effort The Task Takes For This User? Count everything the task asks of the user: the thinking, the clicking, and the checking they will owe once AI is involved. Fewer clicks proves nothing on its own , because a feature can cut clicks and still leave the person working harder. Write down the cost even when it goes up, since Question 2 may find a return that pays for it. articles.title: IBM Announces IBM Quantum Nighthawk r3: A New Processor to Support 10k Quantum Operations on 520 Programmable Qubits
articles.content: IBM has announced IBM Quantum Nighthawk r3 , its next superconducting quantum processor. It is designed to run 10,000 quantum operations accurately across 520 programmable qubits. In 2027, IBM plans to link 2 r3 chips into a single 1,040-qubit system. For developers, the announcement is speed. The current Nighthawk r2 already runs workloads up to 19x faster than IBM’s earlier processors. TL;DR Size: Nighthawk r3: 520 programmable qubits, 2,034 physical qubits, 10 l-couplers. Nighthawk r2 (live today): 120 programmable qubits, 218 couplers. Runs on: IBM Quantum Platform cloud (r2 as ibm_phoenix ). Superconducting chips in dilution refrigerators, paired with laptop-to-supercomputer classical compute. Performance: r2 executes 100,000+ circuits per second, about 25x Heron, with Heron-class gate fidelity. Best: Up to 19x speedup over earlier IBM processors on partner workloads; E.ON reports 15x. Worst: r3 is a design, not shipping hardware. Chip-to-chip links average 99% state transfer fidelity, short of the 99.9% target. Bottom line: Best: real throughput gains on a cloud chip you can use now. Worst: the 1,040-qubit system is a 2027 plan, not a result. What is IBM Quantum Nighthawk? Nighthawk is IBM’s square-lattice processor family built for quantum advantage workloads. Most qubits connect to 4 nearest neighbors, versus 2 or 3 on earlier designs. That connectivity lets circuits express more entangling structure with fewer swap operations. The current production chip is Nighthawk r2 . It has 120 programmable qubits, 218 couplers and 120 reset elements. That is 458 physical quantum elements in total. How does Nighthawk r2 get 25x more throughput? The bottleneck was qubit reset. Heron uses conditional reset: measure, then flip any qubit found in the excited state. That method cannot fix leaked qubits, so the chip idles for hundreds of microseconds between shots. Nighthawk r2 replaces this with a dissipative reset gadget per qubit. A tunable coupler links each qubit to a cold environment on demand. This drops effective T1 from about 200 microseconds to roughly 25 nanoseconds. Idle time between runs falls to as little as 1 microsecond. The result is 100,000+ circuits per second. Heron manages roughly 4,000. IBM also reports about 25x lower initialization error, while neighbors stay undisturbed. What speedups are partners reporting? According to IBM, clients have run 34 billion circuits on Nighthawk r2 so far. The figures below are self-reported by IBM and its partners. E.ON: 15x speedup in quantum machine learning for energy grid optimization, versus Heron. Oak Ridge National Laboratory: 12x speedup on a magnetic materials simulation matching neutron scattering data. Algorithmiq: circuits ran 8x faster than the original Heron experiment. IBM estimates tensor-network methods need 240x more memory to match. Q-CTRL: a 60-qubit fermionic simulation with 4,497 two-qubit gates. Runtime fell from 4 minutes 25 seconds to 23 seconds. Deviation from the Heron r3 baseline stayed under 1%. IBM also reports accurate observable estimation on circuits with 7,500+ gates, a 2026 roadmap milestone. What changes in Nighthawk r3? Nighthawk r3 keeps r2’s square lattice and fast operations. It scales to 520 programmable qubits from 2,034 physical qubits. It adds 10 chip-to-chip interconnects called l-couplers. Those links are the path to 1,040 qubits. IBM connected 2 Nighthawk r1 chips with 4 l-couplers, each using an 80 cm cable. State transfer fidelity reached up to 99.3%, averaging 99%. IBM also linked 2 cryogenic modules , reaching below 15 millikelvin in under 5 days. How does IBM Quantum Platform mix quantum and classical compute? IBM Quantum Platform now runs HPC and quantum jobs in one managed environment. Users can attach classical compute from a laptop, a supercomputer or the platform itself. articles.title: Power Grids On 5 Continents Pulse Every 60s. Scientists Think They Know Why
articles.content: "ScienceAlert is reporting that researchers may have finally determined why, for many years, power grids around the world have been pulsing every 60 seconds," writes longtime Slashdot reader fahrbot-bot. The likely culprit? Uninterruptible power supplies running routine battery checks. From the report: Every minute, some uninterruptible power supplies perform routine battery checks, creating small but measurable surges in electricity demand. And it's like clockwork. "Even benign control routines can become systemically relevant when many devices act coherently," writes a team led by physicist Dirk Witthaut of the University of Cologne, Germany, in a paper published in Nature Energy. "Unintended synchronization can generate recurrent and potentially amplified oscillatory behavior in large-scale cyber-physical energy systems." To figure it out, Witthaut and his colleagues analyzed high-resolution electricity measurements from buildings at the Forschungszentrum Julich research campus in Germany. [... they found that] the 60-second pattern appeared in four buildings, all of which contained uninterruptible power supplies. None of the buildings they measured without these systems showed the same pattern. Following the electrical signals more closely, the researchers detected tiny bursts of current from the batteries at precisely one-minute intervals. They were able to trace the resulting fluctuations through one building's electrical system, all the way to the connection with the public high-voltage grid. The manufacturer subsequently confirmed the culprit's identity -- routine battery self-tests, conducted automatically by the systems' management software. But why would equipment in different buildings, let alone different countries, be doing this at the same time? The answer appears to lie in the clocks. Digital devices can synchronize their internal clocks using external time signals, meaning that independently operating systems can end up performing their scheduled tasks together. Individually, these small checks are insignificant. But when enough devices act in synchrony, their combined electricity demand can produce a measurable effect across an entire power grid. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: 'The Good Daughter' review: Meghann Fahy and Rose Byrne star in a bingeable Peacock mystery that Harlan Coben fans shouldn't skip
articles.content: Tom's Guide Verdict: “The Good Daughter” Rating: 3/5 Stars Verdict: "Based on the thriller novel by Karin Slaughter, 'The Good Daughter' is a twist-filled mystery set in a small Georgia town across dual time periods. Meghann Fahy and Rose Byrne anchor the story as estranged sisters, delivering family relationship drama that is more satisfying than the pulpy, convoluted Harlan Coben-like plot." Premiere date/time: All six episodes premiere Nov. 12 Where to watch: Stream on Peacock Although she has a long way to go before reaching Harlan Coben status, novelist Karin Slaughter creates similarly addictive yet disposable crime thrillers, full of sudden twists and complicated backstory. I get a similar feeling from watching TV adaptations of both authors’ books, eager to tune in for the next episode but a bit let down when all of the secrets are revealed. That was my response to the first TV series based on a Slaughter novel, the 2022 Netflix hit “Pieces of Her,” and it’s the same for the new Slaughter series, "The Good Daughter." There’s more emotional depth to Slaughter’s stories than Coben’s, and “The Good Daughter” is anchored by two strong performances from Meghann Fahy and Rose Byrne as estranged sisters Charlie and Sam Quinn. The six-episode Peacock original series, adapted by Slaughter herself from her 2017 novel, is more briskly paced than “Pieces of Her,” although it still gets bogged down in lengthy stretches of exposition. It deals with some heavy themes, but always in a pulpy, airport-novel kind of way, making it an easy binge despite the dark subject matter. ‘The Good Daughter’ explores dangerous small-town secrets Set in the fictional Georgia town of Pikeville, “The Good Daughter” shifts between past and present as it tells the connected stories of two terrible incidents involving Charlie and Sam (played as children by Drew Cheek and Audrey Grace Marshall). Their father Rusty (Brendan Gleeson) is a steadfast local defense attorney who frequently incurs the wrath of the corrupt legal system run by the powerful Coin family. When he angers the wrong people, the Quinns’ house gets burned down, and then they’re attacked by two gunmen in their new home while Rusty is out. The assailants kill Charlie and Sam’s mother, Gamma (Olivia Williams), and the two young girls barely get away. (Image credit: Mark Hill / Peacock) Decades later, Charlie still lives in Pikeville, working as a defense lawyer alongside her father and separated from her husband Ben (Michael Dorman), an assistant district attorney. She finds herself in the wrong place at the wrong time when she witnesses the aftermath of a shooting at the local high school, and soon she’s deeply involved in defending the shooter, a scared and possibly mentally disabled young woman named Kelly Wilson (Shayna Benardo). After he’s incapacitated, Rusty calls in Sam for help, and she arrives from New York City, where she’s been working as a patent lawyer. That’s just some of the set-up for this overstuffed story, which can get a bit unwieldy as it moves back and forth across time periods and works out all of the intricate, overlapping relationships among the characters. Of course, everyone in town is hiding something, and that includes the Quinns, who have to reveal their own long-buried secrets while searching for the truth about what actually happened at the high school, where the principal and one student were shot dead. The central relationship carries ‘The Good Daughter’ (Image credit: Mark Hill / Peacock) In the hands of lesser actors, “The Good Daughter” could have come across as low-rent exploitation, but Fahy and Byrne find the honesty and vulnerability in their characters, and the show succeeds as a story about sisters learning to trust and care for each other again. As the present-day story begins, Charlie and Sam haven’t seen each other in 10 years, and Sam initially intends to spend only a day in town to help Rusty get back on his feet. But the more they’re together,…
articles.author: Josh Bell

articles.titleFa: مروری بر سریال «دختر خوب»: میگن فاهی و رز بایرن در یک رازآلودگی بیننده‌پسند در پیکاک
articles.summaryFa: سریال «دختر خوب» بر اساس رمان مهیج کارین اسلاوتر ساخته شده و داستان دو خواهر جداافتاده را در یک شهر کوچک در جورجیا روایت می‌کند. این سریال با بازی میگن فاهی و رز بایرن، داستانی پر از پیچ و تاب را ارائه می‌دهد که ابعاد عاطفی بیشتری نسبت به داستان‌های هارلان کوبن دارد. همه شش قسمت این سریال از ۱۲ نوامبر در پیکاک پخش خواهد شد.
articles.summaryEn: The series "The Good Daughter" is based on the thriller novel by Karin Slaughter and tells the story of two estranged sisters in a small Georgia town. Starring Meghann Fahy and Rose Byrne, it offers a twist-filled narrative with more emotional depth than Harlan Coben's stories. All six episodes premiere on November 12 on Peacock.
insightsFa: موضوع سریال درباره خواهران جداافتاده و رازهای کوچک شهر است.
بازیگران اصلی میگن فاهی و رز بایرن عملکرد خوبی دارند.
سریال دارای پیچ و تاب‌های جذاب و عاطفی است.
تاریخ انتشار سریال ۱۲ نوامبر و در پیکاک قابل مشاهده است.
این سریال به درک عمیق‌تری از رابطه خانوادگی می‌پردازد.
articles.whyItMattersFa: این خبر مهم است زیرا «دختر خوب» با تأکید بر پیچیدگی‌های روابط خانوادگی و رازهای کوچک شهر، می‌تواند بینندگان را به خود جلب کند و به بحث درباره رمان‌های مهیج دامن بزند.

articles.title: Nebuly raises $21M Series A to measure the ROI of enterprise AI
articles.content: Nebuly, a Turin-based company that helps businesses measure the financial return from their AI agents, has raised $21m in a Series A round led by Planven. Exor Ventures, Tenacity Capital, TGVG Capital and Fastweb+Vodafone also participated, alongside CDP Venture Capital’s AI and Digital Transition funds. articles.titleFa: شرکت نبولی با جذب ۲۱ میلیون دلار سرمایه، بازگشت سرمایه هوش مصنوعی را اندازه‌گیری می‌کند
articles.summaryFa: شرکت نبولی مستقر در تورین، که به کسب‌وکارها در اندازه‌گیری بازگشت مالی از ایجنت‌های هوش مصنوعی کمک می‌کند، در یک دور سرمایه‌گذاری سری A به مبلغ ۲۱ میلیون دلار جذب کرده است. این دور سرمایه‌گذاری به رهبری پلانون صورت گرفته و شرکت‌های دیگری نظیر Exor Ventures و Tenacity Capital نیز در آن مشارکت داشته‌اند.
articles.summaryEn: Nebuly, a Turin-based company that helps businesses measure the financial return from their AI agents, has raised $21 million in a Series A funding round led by Planven. Other participants in the round include Exor Ventures, Tenacity Capital, and TGVG Capital, showcasing the growing importance of measuring AI ROI for companies.
insightsFa: نبولی بر روی اندازه‌گیری بازگشت سرمایه هوش مصنوعی تمرکز دارد.
بازار سرمایه‌گذاری در حوزه هوش مصنوعی به سرعت در حال رشد است.
جذب ۲۱ میلیون دلار نشان‌دهنده اعتماد سرمایه‌گذاران به نوآوری‌های این حوزه است.
شرکت‌های بزرگی نظیر Exor Ventures در این دور مشارکت داشته‌اند.
امروزه بسیاری از شرکت‌ها به دنبال ارزیابی اثرات مالی هوش مصنوعی هستند.
articles.whyItMattersFa: این خبر نشان می‌دهد که اندازه‌گیری تأثیر مالی هوش مصنوعی به عنوان یک نیاز ضروری برای شرکت‌ها در حال مطرح شدن است، و این امر می‌تواند تأثیر عمیقی در تصمیم‌گیری‌های سرمایه‌گذاری هوش مصنوعی داشته باشد.
